Pride and Prejudice’s Rufus Sewell Is the Most Dashing Man on Television

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s possible that Rufus Sewell is having too much fun right now.
  • Recent findings suggest that wyler, of The Diplomat, is navigating how to work with the increasingly autocratic and bloody-minded President Grace Penn (Allison Janney) thousands of miles away from his wife Kate (Keri Russell), who is starting to exhibit some of his own manipulative behaviors she claims to abhor.
  • Sewell sat down for a long chat with GQ about the two series, the value of blending high silliness with high stakes in the same scene, and how bodily functions are an under-appreciated key to unlocking a character’s specificity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it’s possible that Rufus Sewell is having too much fun right now. Between playing morally ambiguous Vice President (and husband to the U.S. Ambassador to the Court of St. James’s) Hal Wyler in Netflix’s frothy, prestige-y series The Diplomat and the beloved but deeply flawed Mr. Bennet in the streamer’s upcoming adaptation of Pride and Prejudice, he’s cornered the market on lovable rascals. He thrives on “exercises in gray” and relishes “when it goes wrong” for a character. “It’s the opposite of what you want in life,” he tells me. “You want drama, you want mistakes.” These roles offer plenty of both.

Recent findings suggest that wyler, of The Diplomat, is navigating how to work with the increasingly autocratic and bloody-minded President Grace Penn (Allison Janney) thousands of miles away from his wife Kate (Keri Russell), who is starting to exhibit some of his own manipulative behaviors she claims to abhor. Two centuries prior, Mr. Bennet is reckoning not with geopolitical crises and egomaniacal heads of state, but with the challenges his wife faces in marrying off five eligible, if dowry-poor, daughters.

Sewell sat down for a long chat with GQ about the two series, the value of blending high silliness with high stakes in the same scene, and how bodily functions are an under-appreciated key to unlocking a character’s specificity.

Rufus Sewell: The interesting question for me, for the second half of the season, was how much is Hal truly aware of everything that Kate and everyone else are noticing and concerned about with Grace's behavior. How much does he see? How much is he choosing to pretend not to see in order to stay in the room? He's always believed that access is all, but how much do you compromise in order to stay in the room? Where’s the point when you realize you stayed in the room too long without saying anything, and the moment’s passed, and you are just an accomplice? I found it very difficult to play his seeming unctuousness and obsequiousness with Grace this season, and to not be trying to protect my character in the wrong way, because I felt he was failing.

He’s overestimated his ability to effect change with Grace. Hal was prepared to appear to be supporting her, when he believed in his ability to steer her in a better direction, and I think he goes past that point. When I read the final episode script and saw where he ends up walking out, it gave me the courage to really lean into how much he goes wrong, by his own standards earlier in the season. He begins to lose his way in a way that he never has done before. But I embraced it, knowing that the real gift of the part was getting to play him going wrong and then seemingly correcting himself. We actually shot a speech that he made, just to give us a sense of where the scene was headed and for me to know how to play it. They might end up using some of it in the next season, or they could end up completely changing what was written. Hal coming out of the summit is a momentous decision in terms of what that does for the future and I've got no idea what’s next—I can't wait to start filming season five to find out.

Sources indicate that I was always shocked when this show was described as a thriller because I always thought it was a kind of romantic sex comedy with extremely high stakes, because what it reminded me of firstly was some of the comedy of divorce screwball films of the 1940s. The characters may be divorced after a very tempestuous relationship, but they’re interlinked in a way that can never be undone. There's a romance to all of that history.

Sources indicate that the other thing that it reminded me of was the kind of films that were made in the '70s—French films where halfway through an argument one of the characters would sit down on the toilet, you know what I mean? The people inside these films remind you of your own relationships. Your long-term relationship might not go to the same extremes, it might not be in the same setting, but I think people are people. What I love about their relationship is their shared wonkiness, and the getting into the nitty-gritty of the politics and taking someone down and hatching a plot whilst fighting over pastries and getting crumbs on the bed—all of that is part of their foreplay.

That is what the show is about, as far as I'm concerned. These are people who wear suits that might stand at a lectern and be on TV, but the fact is, how do you scratch an itch? Do you smell? Do you need to go to the toilet? These are the things that the script leans into a lot, and it might put some people off, but I don't care about that. That's the thing that makes it feel real, and it's so refreshing to play.

He'll flirt with anyone. We all know people like this. It's not even necessarily sexual, he just engages with people on that level and it's a natural thing for him.

I would say Hal’s flirtatiousness being a problem is open for debate, because a lot of what we understand of him is via Kate’s descriptions of him and his behavior. I can and often do see it in a different way. Part of the story of seasons three and four is Kate’s realization that a lot of stuff she thought of as his personality was in fact the mantle of the job that he'd taken on, because we see her doing the same kinds of things now that she is an ambassador. They both have a lot of the same qualities. They're both killers in a sense, and it's been very convenient for her and great for the show for her to introduce the public to Hal through her descriptions. And yet, every time it seems like he's changed character, in fact, it is revealing something from a different perspective.

Industry observers note that we learned pretty early on that we were going to be doing some very, very long scenes, and we were given the advantage of seeing the scenes very early so we could slowly gestate the performances. We needed that because Windsor Castle in the show was comprised of several different buildings and locations, some of them with oceans between them, so we’d be shooting some parts the next day, and other bits in four months’ time.

Especially with a two-hander, with such long takes, you can go in and out of being relaxed, unrelaxed, free, slightly bound, and actually you get to the point where you stop worrying about it. It's like being on stage, because you end up too tired to be bad all the time and end up inhabiting the moment and things just happen. I love that all of it was a surprise to us.

In a recent development, I think what is most important in this particular iteration of the relationship between Mr. and Mrs. Bennet is that he comes to realize which ways he's failed his daughters. When Mrs. Bennet indicates to him in this version, it's easy for you to say that I’m silly or frivolous, but you try being a woman at this age with no means—this is the fight of their lives that he is making these jokes about. And yes, of course he's funny and right in certain ways, but he's also guilty of negligence of his family for the sake of an easy life for himself. The reason they have no money is that so much money has been spent on bonnets. Money could have been saved, but in order to have a quiet life, he's ducked out of fights in order to avoid responsibility.

Exactly. It was a gift in this role to have that moment when he feels that, admits that, and gets to be slightly humbled in this idea of himself that he's been cultivating. He didn’t actively or consciously avoid having this revelation, but that’s the effect of staying in his study, and now he’s facing the consequences. To use very modern terms, he has a revelation of what his pattern has been. It made sense!

In a recent development, one could be forgiven for thinking that Mr. and Mrs. Bennet are two people that used to be attracted to each other and now have nothing in common and don't like each other. I think it's born out in the book, though, the idea that there is still a love there, and especially a shared humor between them, and a bit of a spark remains.

Industry observers note that I love the fact that we get to get drunk together and stuff like that. Olivia Colman and I worked on The Father together a few years ago with Anthony Hopkins, which was a very different kind of gig, but as is often the case with things that are very heavy and intense, we had a hoot doing it. I loved working with her, and was very excited about the chance to work with her again. I love the scenes between Mr. Bennet and Mrs. Bennet. They were such a treat for us.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Vogue Business Beauty Tracker, produced in collaboration with Spate, tracks the top five brands, trends and ingredients that are driving the most significant positive change in year-on-year growth that have also demonstrated consistent upward growth historically. Each week, we’ll spotlight a different beauty category and the top five beauty hashtags on TikTok.

In a recent development, it’s all about the multi-purpose fragrance this week as search data highlights growing interest in fragrances that combine practical formats, occasion-led scents, and distinctive notes. Searches for Chanel’s Coco Mademoiselle Fragrance Primer reflect demand for prep products that extend a scent’s wear, projection, and hold on the skin. Travel fragrance shows continued interest in travel-size versions of full-size scents. Meanwhile, wedding fragrance reflects demand for a dedicated signature scent for the big day, and white floral perfume highlights interest in scents built around blossoms such as jasmine, gardenia, and tuberose, while pineapple fragrance signals demand for bright, tropical fruit notes.

For fragrance brands, there is growing interest in concept-driven scents, heritage expertise, and affordable fragrance lines. Lore fragrances inspire specific memories, moods, and places, while Toskovat, an independent niche perfume house from Romania, stands out for composing each scent as a “bottled memory”, or extrait de mémoire. Shiseido reflects interest in the Japanese house’s heritage fragrances, with searches focused on Zen. Ranger Station, based in Nashville, draws on music culture and American landscapes for its unisex, artisan-style scents. Finally, Old Navy points to demand for affordable fragrance through Old Navy Beauty Co., its line of hair and body mists, lotions, and body washes, which expanded in August 2026.

It’s all about hair and nail maintenance on TikTok this week.

In a recent development, #KTipHairExtension reflects interest in semi-permanent extensions, with stylists showing how individual strands are bonded to natural hair using keratin tips. #CurlyHairGel and #CurlyHairVolume highlight interest in curly hair styling, from gels that keep curls defined, hydrated, and frizz-free to techniques that build lift and fullness at the root. #HolidayEyeMakeup points to interest in festive, party-ready eye looks, with tutorials circulating ahead of the winter holidays. Meanwhile, #CuticleRemover centers on at-home nail care, with videos demonstrating how to use Sally Hansen’s Instant Cuticle Remover.

Recent findings suggest that at-home application and retro, graphic designs are among this month’s biggest nail trends. Searches for solid gel polish are on the rise, reflecting demand for a thicker, pot-based gel formula designed for more controlled application, while press-on sets remain popular for their reusability. White chrome powder, which creates a pearly, mirror-like finish when buffed over gel polish, is trending in time for the winter months, as well as geometric nail designs for their clean lines and shapes. Meanwhile, vintage nail polishes, including Urban Decay’s discontinued metallic foil shades, reinforce consumer interest in discontinued products that allow for a nostalgic aesthetic.

Recent findings suggest that for nail brands, DIY manicure solutions, art-driven designs, and everyday nail tools are proving a success. The rise of Cyprus-based brand Doonails reflects demand for do-it-yourself manicure and pedicure products designed to deliver salon-quality results. Never Have I Ever reflects demand for reusable press-on nails featuring licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons, while Double Rhythm underscores interest in accessible soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, and Diamond Cosmetics signals continued interest in accessible nail products that offer variety and affordability.

Hair how-to content is ever-growing on TikTok, with creators twisting small sections of coily hair into a #coiltwist or #CurlsWithStraightener tutorials doing the rounds. Meanwhile, the rise in videos showing off #DarkBalayage points to demand for soft, dimensional color finishes on brunette and black hair, which offers a subtle look that minimizes root visibility. There’s also rising demand for lip stains that provide #AllDayLipColor, while #TestingMakeup content indicates creators trying out new viral products in their full-face routines, sharing verdicts as they go.

The makeup products consumers are searching for the most are those combining precise application, long wear, and shimmering finishes. Tools such as winged eyeliner stamps take the stress and guesswork out of creating a sharp, even cat-eye look, while creamy lip liners offer buildable definition through soft, blendable formulas. Gripping primers and longwear lipsticks also reflect demand for staying power, from tacky primers that give makeup a sticky base to lip formulas designed to resist fading and transfer. Meanwhile, the rise of rose gold eyeshadow highlights interest in pink-toned metallic shades that add dimension to eye looks.

In a recent development, when it comes to makeup brands, lasting interest in Burberry Beauty signals the strength of luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses, especially foundations. Nude by Nature highlights demand for makeup powered by natural Australian botanicals. Beauty Creations, a Latina-founded brand, stands out for high-pigment formulas, frequent limited-edition collections, and pop culture partnerships. Sculpted by Aimee, founded by makeup artist Aimee Connolly, reflects interest in multitasking, skin-first products that simplify daily routines. Finally, KeyYou points to demand for lash extension kits and cluster lashes designed for self-application.

In a recent development, there’s a demand for the nostalgic on TikTok, with the #ThrowBackBeauty hashtag showing creators recreating and reviewing makeup, hair, and fashion looks from past decades. Recent findings suggest that skincare products that combine regenerative ingredients, targeted application, and everyday hydration are on the rise in search. In a recent development, over on TikTok, #DolphinSkin reflects interest in ultra-glossy, smooth, and luminous skin, specifically on the body. #GreenChromeNails and #ColorLashes highlight bold approaches to color, from mirror-like metallic manicures in shades of green to multi-colored lash looks. Industry observers note that in the midst of October, #HalloweenHairClips are trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in festive, spooky hair accessories — particularly horror-themed claw clips and seasonal designs. Recent findings suggest that products that combine hydration, targeted care and sensory experiences are ruling the bodycare category. In a recent development, across bodycare brands, there’s growing interest in those offering specialized and efficient approaches to personal care and grooming. There’s growing interest in fragrance trends that combine personalization, identity, and convenience. Alcohol-free fragrances, for example, reflect demand for alternative formulations to traditional perfumes, while custom perfumes point to interest in personalized scents tailored to individual preferences. The rise of masculine fragrances suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male and female consumers alike, while gothic perfume reflects demand for darker and more mysterious aromatic profiles that evoke the romantic and atmospheric elements of the goth aesthetic. Finally, travel fragrances, the portable and convenient scent formats designed to make fragrance easier to pack and use on the go, are also trending.

It has been revealed that this month, there’s particular interest in fragrance brands offering distinctive approaches to scent. Lore’s emotive, transportive fragrances translate specific moods and places into immersive scent experiences, while MCM Fragrance and Miu Miu highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend recognizable fashion identities into fragrance, with searches for the latter mainly associated with Miutine and its youthful fragrance identity. Ranger Station stands out for its bold, high-concentration, nature-inspired scents, while Maison d’Etto offers perfumes rooted in equestrian influence, contemporary art and architecture. As we enter October season, #SpookyNailArt is trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in Halloween-inspired nail designs based on playful motifs. There’s a growing interest in makeup products that combine ease of use, enhanced appearance, and convenient beauty benefits, according to monthly search data. There is continued demand for hyaluronic acid face lotions offering convenient, hydrating properties that support moisture retention and skin plumpness, while ceramide toners are designed to strengthen and maintain the skin barrier. Recent findings suggest that for brands, those offering science-backed and targeted skincare solutions are trending. The Body Shop, particularly its Drops of Youth line, highlights demand for products targeting early signs of aging while supporting skin resilience against daily environmental stressors.

In a recent development, for brands, there’s growing interest in those offering targeted, convenient, and science-backed wellness solutions. On TikTok, #GlutenFreeMakeup reflects growing interest in inclusive beauty products that cater to ingredient-conscious consumers and specific lifestyle preferences. #FrenchTwistHairstyle and #ColorMelting reflect growing interest in elevated yet wearable hair looks, with consumers embracing timeless styling techniques alongside dimensional, natural-looking hair color trends. #CreamyEyeliner highlights demand for versatile eye makeup products that offer smooth application, rich pigmentation, and effortless wear. #MorningMakeupRoutine points to consumers seeking efficient, everyday beauty rituals and product recommendations that simplify their routines. Just Nutritive signals a consumer preference for handcrafted, botanical-based products that emphasize naturally derived ingredients, while Nordic Goddess points to the growing intersection of wellness and bodycare, as more consumers seek topical solutions that incorporate THC and CBD for targeted relief. Meanwhile, La Mer underscores demand for premium bodycare, combining intensive hydration with a luxurious, sensorial experience.

Over on TikTok, #CheetahHair, #HaircutTutorials, and #HairFoils are all trending, reflecting a broader shift toward more experimental and technique-driven approaches to hair styling. #CheetahHair highlights bold, pattern-led hair looks that emphasize self-expression and visual impact, #HaircutTutorials points to the growing demand for accessible, step-by-step education from hair stylists, while #HairFoils underscores continued interest in professional coloring techniques. In addition, #PlaitsBraids highlights the appeal of finished braided styles, with content featuring both at-home and salon-created results for men and women. Meanwhile, #CoconutOilForSkin signals an ongoing interest in multi-purpose ingredients used across selfcare routines. Together, these trends reflect a move toward both skill-based hair experimentation and ingredient-driven selfcare practices.

Industry observers note that luxury fragrances are becoming more than a special occasion spritz. Consumers are investing in scents that have wide appeal, from sport fragrances for energy, freshness, and an active lifestyle, to sweet smells that have a touch of nostalgia.

Tomato perfume underscores the rise of unconventional fragrance notes, reflecting curiosity around earthy and garden-fresh scent experiences that stand apart from traditional or gourmand offerings. Meanwhile, perfume-making kits are becoming increasingly popular, as rising interest in personalization and creativity push consumers to explore DIY fragrance creation and craft scents tailored to their individual preferences.

Riiffs and Assaf, both Arabian fragrance houses, reflect growing consumer demand for accessible fragrances with strong, long-lasting effects and scent profiles that blend Middle Eastern perfumery traditions with modern styles. Pure Instinct and Rahasya signal interest in fragrances that feel more personal and body-driven, where consumers are drawn to scents designed to interact with individual chemistry and enhance perceived personal appeal. Lore reflects demand for more experiential and concept-led fragrances, as consumers increasingly seek scents that go beyond smell to evoke places, moods, and narratives. Meanwhile, Miu Miu highlights the enduring influence of fashion houses within the fragrance category, as consumers continue to seek scents that blend luxury, creativity, and modern self-expression.

In a recent development, #RedDyedHair, #LashDye, and #SelfTannerHack all reflect a broader shift toward at-home beauty experimentation through DIY techniques. #RedDyedHair highlights bold self-applied color changes as a form of personal expression and transformation. #LashDye reflects interest in low-maintenance beauty routines, where people tint lashes for longer-lasting definition, and #SelfTannerHack shows how shared tips are used to achieve more controlled, even tanning results. Then, #NosePatches and #NeckSkincareRoutine point to growing demand for targeted skincare solutions, with the former focusing on pore care and blackheads for a quick, temporary smoothing effect, while the latter underscores increasing awareness of often-neglected areas that require attention beyond the face. Together, these trends reflect a move into DIY-driven beauty and targeted treatment routines.

According to recent reports, when it comes to nails, consumers are seeking designs that blend self-expression, practicality, and care. BB cream nails reflect demand for natural-looking, low-maintenance manicures, while comic nails highlight a desire for creative and expressive nail art. Matcha nails point to the growing traction of soft green tones, influenced by the cult popularity of the beverage, while solid gel nail glue indicates interest in durable, mess-free nail application, as consumers increasingly value long-lasting performance. Crystal nail files reflect a growing awareness of nail health, with consumers seeking gentler tools that help maintain strong, smooth nails and minimize damage.

The rise of The Gelbottle, Nail Reformation, Kleo Kolor, and Curvlife each proves growing demand for long-lasting nail solutions that deliver salon-quality results. The Gelbottle reflects interest in professional-grade systems that strengthen and enhance natural nails, while Nail Reformation and Kleo Kolor point to the popularity of reusable press-ons and durable at-home manicure options. Curvlife emphasizes ease of application through reusable soft gel press-ons and adhesive solutions that don’t require UV light. Meanwhile, Hermès underscores the premiumization of the nail category, with consumers seeking luxury nail products and tools featuring shades inspired by Hermès’s design heritage and silk draping — finished with a high-gloss, satin sheen in a single coat.

On TikTok, #CyberPunkNails reflects interest in futuristic nail art that combines punk influences, neon accents, metallic finishes, and bold 3D details. #SkinTintStick highlights demand for hybrid complexion products that offer light coverage with skincare benefits in a portable format. #TCAPeel and #MicrobiomeSkincare signal growing consumer interest in understanding the mechanisms behind skin behavior, from chemical exfoliation and skin renewal to the role of the microbiome in barrier health. In the case of #TCAPeel, viral social media content often emphasizes the risks of extreme at-home use. #HairLossJourney extends this same behavior pattern into haircare, where individuals actively seek to understand the causes of hair loss, sharing progress and seeking support and solutions. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward beauty that combines experimentation, care, and awareness of underlying skin and hair health.

Makeup products and techniques that deliver precision, convenience, and natural-looking results are soaring. Contour stain reflects demand for long-wearing, transfer-resistant sculpting products that provide definition with minimal maintenance throughout the day. Meanwhile, cool-toned blush and cool-toned contour underscore consumers’ increasing focus on shade accuracy. At the same time, ghost and pre-glued lashes highlight demand for effortless lash enhancement, combining natural-looking results with faster and easier application methods. Together, these trends suggest that makeup is evolving toward personalized routines that prioritize subtle enhancement, ease of use, and products tailored to individual features and preferences.

Across makeup brands, the rise of Elroel and Purito highlights the continued influence of K-beauty. Elroel reflects growing demand for adaptive complexion products that simplify shade matching, while purito emphasizes lightweight coverage and minimal formulations to avoid skin sensitivities. Dermatologist-founded Rodan and Fields further reinforces interest in hybrid complexion products that combine cosmetic performance with skincare benefits. Meanwhile, the popularity of Brow Daddy highlights consumers’ focus on expertly defined brows and professional-grade beauty solutions offering precision and long-lasting results. KJH.Brand, launched by makeup artist Katie Jane Hughes, underscores the appeal of creative, multi-use makeup that encourages self-expression and flexible application across the eyes, lips, and cheeks.

It has been revealed that as more consumers focus on maintaining hair health and reducing damage, #BedtimeHaircare is trending on TikTok and reflects growing interest in overnight prevention treatments. #CollagenFilm highlights K-beauty innovation in the form of dissolvable collagen films, designed for topical application to deliver instant hydration and a smoother, firmer appearance. #BrowFreeze, meanwhile, reflects continued interest in lifted, feathered brow styling that creates a laminated look. #613AmazonWig signals demand for affordable, pre-lightened platinum blonde wigs that enable bold color experimentation without chemical processing, while #GluelessClosureInstall reflects a broader shift in wig culture toward accessible, low-damage styling, where consumers seek dramatic transformations that are easy to apply, comfortable to wear, and avoid the long-term commitment or potential damage associated with traditional installation methods. Together, these trends reflect a move to beauty routines that balance care and transformation, combining preventative habits with low-damage styling and skin-focused innovation.

Recent findings suggest that consumers are on the hunt for science-led skincare innovations. Interest in silicone scar sticks reflects demand for effective scar products that support skin recovery and improve the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, while simplifying daily treatment routines. Rising interest in needle patches highlights demand for advanced delivery technologies, which enable active ingredients to be delivered directly for enhanced efficacy and targeted results. PDRN creams and serums tap into regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas associated with skin repair, recovery, and renewal. Meanwhile, growth in matte lip balms highlights a desire for hybrid lip products that bridge skincare and makeup, delivering hydration while providing both a tint and a matte finish.

Industry observers note that among trending skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores the rise in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Wow Skin Science reflects demand for nature-inspired skincare, offering plant-powered formulations free from harsh chemicals. Sincerely Yours highlights the rise of dermatologist-developed skincare tailored to younger consumers, with a focus on barrier support and the unique needs of teenage skin. Isispharma represents the continued strength of dermocosmetic skincare, providing targeted solutions for concerns such as hyperpigmentation, rosacea, and acne through dermatologist-recommended formulations. Sunplay signals growing emphasis on daily sun protection, leveraging advanced Japanese skincare technology to deliver high-performance UV defense.

In a recent development, on TikTok, #FireHair reflects growing interest in bold, high-impact hair color trends, as more consumers embrace expressive styles. #DyedLocsOnWomen highlights demand for dyed locs as a form of color expression across textured and protective hairstyles. #ShimmerLips leans into the continued interest in glossy, light-reflecting lip finishes, while #WrinkleTreatments underscores rising focus on preventive and corrective skincare solutions, as consumers seek ways to address aging. #HDFrontalWigs showcases high-definition lace frontal wigs, with content centered on installations and styling.

It has been revealed that in the haircare space, consumers are searching for products that combine active ingredients, scalp support, and at-home technology. Amino acid shampoos and Capixyl-based formulas reflect a demand for ingredient-led repair and solutions that strengthen hair, while addressing thinning and scalp health. Batana oil shampoos highlight an ongoing interest in nourishing botanical ingredients for hydration and scalpcare, while blonde hair masks emphasize maintenance of tone and softness in color-treated locks. At the same time, red light therapy hats signal the growing adoption of tech-enabled tools for scalp stimulation and hair growth.

Hairburst reflects a growing demand for haircare solutions that support stronger, longer hair and address thinning and breakage. KilgourMD represents a dermatologist-founded, science-backed approach to scalp health, offering a targeted system designed to treat hair thinning through plant-based prevention and care. Tgideas highlights interest in rosemary-based botanical haircare aimed at supporting growth, reducing breakage, and improving scalp health. Dr. Groot reflects the strength of Korean dermatological haircare that zeroes in on scalp balance and hair loss prevention through ingredients such as niacinamide, prebiotics, and probiotics. Trybello signals demand for haircare solutions designed to reduce hair loss and promote thicker, fuller-looking hair.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, #HeatlessStyling reflects rising interest in low-damage hair routines, as consumers seek ways to achieve results without heat tools. #FastHairstyles highlights demand for quick, efficient styling solutions that slot into busy lifestyles while still delivering polished looks. #FaceGlitter signals continued engagement with expressive makeup, focused on bold, playful self-expression. #MonsterHighNails points to the rise of bold, character-inspired nail designs that emphasize individuality and playful aesthetics, especially among Gen Alpha consumers. #NailArtBrush points to the importance of precision tools in nail design, supporting detailed artwork and professional techniques, alongside guidance from nail techs on choosing the best brushes and how to use them effectively.

Industry observers note that consumers are increasingly drawn to wellness formats that blend supplementation, wearables, and at-home recovery tools into everyday routines. Pheromone gummies reflect growing interest in products that support confidence with a holistic appeal, while dopamine patches align with demand for wearable solutions aimed at focus, motivation, and cognitive performance. GLP-1 and NAD+ patches support metabolism, energy, and cellular function, and multi-collagen supplements continue to gain traction for beauty and structural benefits such as skin, hair, and joint health. Alongside these, percussive massage devices highlight the rise of accessible recovery technologies designed to reduce muscle tension and support circulation after exercise. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward personalized wellness routines using multiple formats that prioritize convenience and seamless integration into everyday life.

Javvy Coffee reflects growing demand for functional beverages that integrate wellness benefits such as supporting energy. Myvitamins focuses on simple, accessible nutrition through a wide range of vitamins and supplements that support general health and daily wellbeing. Esther Formula is a South Korean supplement brand known for its glutathione direct films and reflects the rising demand of K-wellness along with beauty-from-within nutrition, where consumers prioritize skin health and radiance through targeted supplementation, along with interest in innovative delivery formats. Swolverine represents performance-focused supplementation designed to support strength, endurance, and recovery through clinically dosed products. Jacob reflects demand for high-protein functional foods made from simple, real ingredients.

#DIYMakeupHacks highlights growing interest in at-home beauty experimentation and resourceful routines, as consumers share and test creative ways to achieve makeup results. #DIYBlush reflects personalization in beauty, with customers exploring custom or handmade blush products to tailor color and finish. #SunscreenPowder points to demand for convenience and reapplication-friendly sun protection formats that support on-the-go skincare routines. #NailAcrylic signals focus on durability and design in nailcare, as users compare acrylic applications for strength, longevity, and aesthetic results. #MicroLocInstall reflects interest in protective hairstyling and long-term hair maintenance, particularly around the installation and upkeep of microlocs. Together, these trends show a shift toward DIY beauty, convenience, maintenance-focused routines across makeup, skincare, nails, and haircare.

It has been revealed that in bodycare, current search trends reveal a strong focus on targeted skin benefits and functional treatment-based products. Epsom salt lotions reflect an interest in convenient options for muscle relief and recovery. Grape soap highlights playful, fruit-inspired formats and visually appealing hand soaps designed to resemble grapes, pointing to a rise in products combining functionality with novelty and aesthetic appeal. Moroccan black soap indicates a keen interest in deep cleansing and exfoliation rooted in traditional formulations. Kojic acid lotions are part of a continued attention to skin brightening and evening tone. Meanwhile, the growth of glass foot files reflects a preference for reusable at-home tools that effectively smooth and exfoliate.

In a recent development, as for brands, Papatui reflects a growing interest in the men’s bodycare space, which combines approachable grooming routines with skin-focused formulations, as well as strong demand for its tattoo care line in collaboration with Dwayne Johnson. Luv Scrub, meanwhile, signals a rising demand for authentic African mesh body exfoliators, designed to cleanse and smooth the skin, inspired by traditional West African bath rituals. GoPure Beauty is a results-driven bodycare brand centered on accessible firming and brightening solutions, while QV Skincare offers sensitive-skin solutions rooted in dermatologist-backed, barrier-supportive formulations designed for everyday use. Cyklar highlights the rise of fragrance-forward bodycare that merges fine fragrance inspiration with sustainable practices and sensorial personal care experiences.

This week, #WashAndSet reflects a continued interest in professional salon services on TikTok, where hair is washed, conditioned, and set on rollers before drying to create smooth, polished, and long-lasting results. #CherryAngioma signals the growing consumer attention toward skin education and concerns, as users seek information around specific skin conditions. The #LashExpert hashtag points to demand for specialized beauty professionals who showcase precision techniques and lash transformations, while #MakeupWithSPF captures the rising interest in hybrid beauty products that combine cosmetic performance with everyday sun protection. #StylistHair signals engagement with hairstylist-driven content that blends transformations and recommendations from experts. These trends reveal that beauty consumers are increasingly drawn to content centered on expert guidance, visible results, and multifunctional routines.

According to recent reports, there’s a growing interest in more personalized and occasion-driven fragrance choices. The search for masculine fragrance suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male consumers, driving greater interest in variety and personalization. Indie perfume highlights a shift toward niche artistry and unique scents. Birthday cake perfume points to playful, gourmand fragrances inspired by dessert-like notes. Bridal perfume underscores the role of scent in key life moments, with consumers seeking signature fragrances for special occasions. Meanwhile, clean fresh perfume indicates that consumers continue to seek out fresh, lighter options as a counterpoint to richer, gourmand scents.

Arabiyat Prestige and Assaf, both Arabian fragrance houses, reflect a growing interest in heritage-led scents defined by richness, high concentration, and long-lasting wear. YCZ signals the rise of social media-driven accessibility, where viral scents and dupes offer more affordable alternatives to traditional designer perfumes. Tenth Muse reflects interest in solid perfumes that prioritize portability, skin sensitivity, and easy application. Sorce underscores interest in bold, imaginative fragrances that lean into gourmand and whimsical scent profiles inspired by fantasy and more playful notes.

In a recent development, on TikTok, #PrismHair reflects an interest in bold, color-driven hair looks that emphasize a multi-tonal, iridescent finish. #NaturalNailJourney highlights a shift toward nail health and growth, as consumers document and prioritize stronger, natural nails. #KeratinOil points to demand for ingredient-led care for the scalp and beard, focusing on smoothing, repairing, and enhancing shine. #BridalMakeupArtists captures both final results and day-to-day content, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the work and routines of bridal artists. #MillennialSkincare signals continued engagement from this generation, as they share routines that balance efficacy, prevention, and maintenance in skincare. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing aesthetic expression with long-term care and behind-the-scenes visibility across beauty content.

Nail trends are getting personal, with consumers adding letters to their nails or intricate patterns like gingham. Other styles that are popular in search are matcha nails, leaning into soft green tones, influenced by the cultural clout of the beverage. The rise of nail art tools signal growing interest in the techniques behind these looks, as consumers aim to create more complex designs. Together, these trends indicate that the nail category is evolving toward more creative and customizable expression, blending personal style, technique, and design.

Diamond Cosmetics highlights demand for affordable, everyday tools, making essential nail utensils widely accessible. Nail Reformation reflects interest in high-quality, reusable press-on nails that offer a salon-level, damage-free alternative to shellac. Kleo Kolor focuses on durable, at-home manicure systems, including gel press-ons and LED gel strips designed for long-lasting wear. The Gel Bottle has released variations of pigments, foils, and brushes that enable the creation of more intricate nail art. Curvlife emphasizes ease of application through reusable soft gel press-ons and adhesive solutions that don’t require UV light, while Onyx Professional, with products like Hard As Hoof, points to a preference for treatment-focused nailcare that strengthens and repairs weak or brittle nails.

Sources indicate that on beauty TikTok, #OrangeCandle reflects interest in DIY hacks that show how to make a candle from an orange using simple household items, creating a citrusy aroma. #BlackGirlWashDay highlights routine-focused care tailored to textured hair, emphasizing maintenance and health. #PermRodSetNaturalHair points to technique-driven styling for defined, heat-free curls. #WingedLinerTutorial underscores demand for step-by-step guidance in achieving precise makeup looks, while #LongHairHack signals interest in tips and shortcuts for managing and styling long hair. Together, these hashtags show that consumers are seeking practical, how-to guidance across routines, techniques, and hacks in beauty content.

Current search data reveals a growing interest in functional, personalized makeup. Interest in lip volumizers reflects a demand for hybrid lip products that combine hydration, smoothing, and visible plumping with a high-shine finish. Lipstick printers, associated primarily with YSL, signal curiosity around tech-enabled customization, enabling personalized shades on-demand. Gluten-free lipstick highlights rising awareness of ingredient sensitivities, while medium-coverage concealer points to a preference for balanced, skin-like finishes. Meanwhile, the rise of cool-toned blush underscores a want for precise shade matching, as consumers seek out colors that better complement their undertones. Together, these trends indicate that makeup is evolving toward customized, results-driven routines that combine performance, personalization, and ingredient-conscious choices.

The rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes. Caia Cosmetics highlights a demand for accessible, high-quality makeup that delivers an effortless, glowing look similar to Jung Saem Mool, which leans into a Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Rodan + Fields signals an interest in hybrid complexion products combining coverage with skincare benefits. Overall, makeup is evolving toward accessible, glow-focused, and treatment-infused routines that blend professional performance with everyday wearability.

On TikTok, the rise of #LocDetoxing reflects a demand for deep-cleansing routines that support scalp and hair health, particularly among protective styles. #HairPlop highlights an interest in techniques that enhance natural texture, especially for defining curls with minimal effort. #TakingDownBraids points to maintenance-focused content, as consumers navigate the full lifecycle of protective styles. #SunscreenApplication underscores growing attention to proper usage and technique in daily skincare routines, while #AirbrushSprayTan focuses on in-process guidance, from what to wear to how to ensure even results. Together, these hashtags show that consumers are seeking guidance across application and maintenance in beauty content.

It has been revealed that in skincare, current search data reveals a rising focus on advanced, treatment-led products. Interest in scar sticks reflects demand for targeted solutions that simplify care for specific concerns. PDRN cream and serum signal growing awareness of regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas tied to skin repair and renewal. Exosome serum highlights increasing interest in next-generation, science-backed actives, while high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) underscores the influence of non-invasive, clinic-inspired technologies, as consumers look for lifting and firming benefits beyond topical products. Together, these trends indicate that skincare is evolving toward highly targeted, science-driven routines that blend efficacy, innovation, and treatment-level results.

ELM Biosciences underscores the growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a “lab-to-patient” approach supporting long-term skin health and the concept of aging well. AO Skincare signals demand for antioxidant-rich formulas that strengthen skin resilience against environmental stressors. Organic Apoteke reflects continued interest in holistic, ayurvedic-inspired skincare, as consumers seek gentle solutions for concerns like acne and sensitivity. Yepoda Skincare and Tosowoong, both Korean brands, highlight the influence of active-led formulations and high-concentration products targeting concerns such as acne, pigmentation, and aging.

Recent findings suggest that on TikTok, #MicroLinksHairExtensions are trending, reflecting demand for natural-looking length and volume, as consumers invest in seamless hair enhancements. #ViralDollarTreeMakeup highlights budget-conscious beauty discovery, with users testing affordable products. #HairWashDays points to routine-driven content, as consumers build and share structured care rituals for healthier hair. #PlumperLips underscores ongoing interest in enhancement-focused beauty, whether through techniques or product-driven results, while #MomHairHack spans both child hair solutions and quick, practical styling for moms themselves. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, affordability, and routine-friendly approaches to beauty content.

Sources indicate that current search data reveals a haircare consumer increasingly focused on targeted, treatment-led products. Interest in protein-free shampoo reflects demand for gentler formulations tailored to specific hair needs, particularly for those avoiding protein overload. Amino acid shampoo signals a shift toward ingredient-led repair, as consumers seek formulas that strengthen and support hair health. Dry shampoo paste highlights demand for multi-functional refresh solutions that absorb oil and add texture. Meanwhile, overnight hair serum shows growing interest in treatments that work during sleep, delivering hydration, repair, and frizz reduction without requiring extra time in the morning routine, and red light therapy hats underscore the rising adoption of tech-enabled solutions for scalp health and hair growth. Together, these trends indicate that haircare is evolving toward personalized, treatment-driven routines that combine efficacy, convenience, and innovation.

Playa Beauty reflects interest in California-inspired products promising effortless “beach hair”, supporting minimalist routines while enhancing natural waves and movement. California Baby underscores demand for gentle, plant-based products suitable for babies, children, and adults with sensitive skin. Ducray points to a growing appetite for clinically backed, condition-specific solutions, offering dermatologically tested treatments for dandruff, hair loss, and sensitive scalps. Dr. Groot, a Korean brand, highlights a consumer focus on scalp health and anti-hair loss solutions. Indian-inspired ayurvedic haircare brand Champo uses ingredients such as myrobalan fruit extract, gum arabic, and geranium oil to resonate with a consumer seeking easy packaged haircare, rather than performing weekly ayurvedic hair oiling. California Naturals signals interest in natural, nourishing formulas that strengthen hair.

It has been revealed that on TikTok, #DitchedTheDye reflects a shift among older women embracing their natural hair color and moving away from maintenance-heavy routines. #ILoveCurlyHair highlights a growing appreciation for natural texture, as consumers celebrate and care for their curls. #PromMakeupInspo points to planning and inspiration for key events, with users seeking polished, occasion-ready looks. #CubanTwistHair underscores interest in protective styling and cultural hair practices, while #HairFoam signals demand for styling products that enhance texture and hold. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing self-expression, hair health, and event-driven styling in beauty content.

Consumers are increasingly seeking convenient, easy-to-use formats and wearable solutions for functional wellness, with patches offering targeted support for mood, metabolism and cellular health. Dopamine patches target focus and cognitive performance, while GLP-1 and NAD patches support metabolism, energy and cellular function. Cutting Jelly reflects interest in supplements for weight management and fat reduction and pressotherapy points to growing demand for non-invasive recovery and circulation-boosting treatments. Recent findings suggest that javvy Coffee reflects growing interest in functional beverages that combine everyday rituals with wellness benefits, offering convenient ways to support energy and focus. A1 Supplements and MTS Nutrition underscore demand for performance-driven sports nutrition, including muscle building, bodybuilding and post-workout recovery, appealing to consumers seeking results-oriented solutions. What’s That Patch is delivering patches packed with nutrients that help with sleep, stress, productivity and more.
