It has been revealed that #LashGlues highlights interest in product performance and comparison between brands, as consumers test glues for reliable, long-lasting lash applications. #MakeupSamples reflects budget-conscious discovery, with shoppers exploring trial sizes and low-commitment ways to test products. #HairTrial points to planning and preparation, as owners test styles ahead of key moments. Meanwhile, #HerbalHairGrowthOil signals demand for natural, treatment-focused solutions, and #BushyBrows spans interest from managing and shaping fuller brows to enhancing volume and testing products. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, planning and creativity in beauty content.

There’s an increasing focus on functional, treatment-led bodycare products that deliver targeted results. Interest in epsom salt lotions reflects a demand for convenient, topical solutions that soothe sore muscles and support recovery. Searches for kojic acid lotions and turmeric body washes signal a growing focus on brightening and tone correction across the body, as consumers turn to ingredient-led solutions that address hyperpigmentation and uneven skin tone. Silicone loofahs and glass foot files point to a preference for hygienic, durable tools that elevate cleansing and exfoliation, while addressing concerns around bacteria and skin safety.

Sources indicate that the rise of Crowned Skin reflects a shift toward multifunctional bodycare, as well as an interest in products like body butter colognes, which combine deep hydration with long-lasting fragrance. Bepanthol highlights demand for clinically backed, multi-purpose solutions that protect and regenerate sensitive or compromised skin. Vermont Soap underscores an interest in gentle, non-irritating cleansers and bar soaps that replace harsher detergents, reflecting a move toward safer, skin-friendly formulations. Meanwhile, Luna Daily and Kate McLeod point to growing desire for specialized and ritualized bodycare — from microbiome-balancing formulas safe for all areas of the body, to waterless, solid moisturizers that emphasize sustainability and sensorial experience.

Recent findings suggest that #CheapBeauty is trending on TikTok, showing that consumers are exploring budget-conscious cosmetic options and highlighting an interest in affordable products. #SkincareComedy reflects engagement with humorous, relatable beauty moments, where audiences enjoy playful takes on everyday experiences. #HairExtensionInstallation points to professional, technique-focused content, as viewers watch skilled stylists demonstrate expert application and installation. Meanwhile, #SkinTighteningTreatment and #VolumeWispy capture aspirational results, from creams that enhance skin firmness to professional lash services that create full, wispy volume, proving that beauty audiences remain captivated by visible, high-impact transformations. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing entertainment, affordability, and aspirational transformations across beauty content.

There’s a craving for gourmand fragrances taking place, as rich, edible-inspired scents capture consumer attention. Searches for masculine fragrances suggest that scent is functioning as an identity marker for male consumers, driving greater interest in variety and personalization. Tomato perfume reflects curiosity around hyper-specific, ingredient-led scents that invite consumers to reimagine familiar smells in a new context. Solid fragrances, meanwhile, point to demand for portable alternatives to spray bottles, where fragrance layering can extend beyond the home. Finally, clean, fresh perfumes reveal how consumers are seeking out fresh, lighter options as a counterpoint to rich, gourmand notes.

The popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a consumer shift toward heritage-rich fragrances known for their high-concentration and long-lasting power. YCZ captures the rise of social media-driven accessibility, proving that viral scents can provide high-quality alternatives to designer perfumes at an affordable price point. Narcotica underscores the appeal of the niche Italian market, where the focus is on “addictive”, high-concentration gourmands that blend bold sweetness with luxurious, long-lasting ingredients.

#TrippyNails are trending, showing that consumers are drawn to surreal, psychedelic nail aesthetics that use distorted patterns and holographic finishes to create eye-catching results. #EasterMakeup reflects a fascination with seasonal, pastel-driven makeup, highlighting how soft color palettes and whimsical details capture attention during spring celebrations. #MakeupCleansingBalm points to growing interest in high-performance cleansers that remove heavy makeup without drying out the skin or leaving it feeling stripped. Meanwhile, #GRWMDate and #HairGoneWrong capture unfiltered, relatable beauty experiences. The former centers on personal storytelling and dating life while getting ready, and the latter highlights the reality of styling mishaps, illustrating how beauty audiences value both the social side of getting ready and the more candid moments that happen along the way.

What’s drawing consumers in? According to data, its playful and creative nail expressions. There’s increased interest in stained glass and matcha nails, as users seek visually striking, color-rich designs that combine artistry with trend-driven aesthetics. Meanwhile, polka dot nails highlight a preference for playful patterns that add personality to everyday manicures. The rise of nail art pens signals a move toward precision and customization. Finally, solid gel nail glue indicates attention to durable, reliable application, showing that consumers value long-lasting performance alongside unique nail looks.

In terms of brands, the rise of Heyhae reflects a shift toward convenient, at-home nail solutions, as more consumers value semi-cured gel strips, which can be applied under natural sunlight for quick, non-toxic manicures. Diamond Cosmetics highlights the demand for affordable, everyday nail tools, making professional-grade manicures accessible to a wide audience. Nail Reformation demonstrates interest in high-quality, reusable press-on nails, offering a salon-level, damage-free experience at home. Meanwhile, Sunuv and IBD Beauty underscore the appeal of salon-level equipment and innovations — from UV and LED lamps to builder gel.

Sources indicate that this week on TikTok, #RobeCurls are trending, as more consumers are drawn to heatless styling techniques that simplify hair routines while delivering defined, natural-looking results. #IceCreamNails reflects a fascination with playful, dessert-inspired nail aesthetics, which underscore how novelty textures and creative color palettes capture attention across nail content. The #LipOilGloss hashtag spotlights lip products that combine shine, nourishment, and a lightweight feel in everyday routines. Meanwhile, #SoftBridalMakeup and #GenZMakeup captures two parallel beauty directions: one centered on polished, natural elegance for milestone events, and the other revealing side-by-side contrasts between Gen Z and millennial makeup styles. Together, these trends show how consumers are balancing practical beauty solutions, playful visual trends, and cross-generational style influences.

Subtle, natural-looking makeup continues to be popularized by medium-coverage products such as concealers. The rise of cool-toned blush and illuminating drops further signals a move toward color theory-informed customization, where consumers use specific undertones and light-reflecting finishes to create a healthy and natural glow. There’s also demand for clean mascara, where lightweight, ingredient-conscious formulas are favored. Another trend on the rise is gluten-free lipsticks, pointing to growing attention to health-conscious formulations.

According to recent reports, the rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Jolie Beauty highlights the demand for alternative, high-performance makeup that allows bold self-expression while remaining vegan and cruelty-free. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes, while Jung Saem Mool underscores the appeal of luxury Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Meanwhile, Concrete Minerals signals a move toward transparent formulations with bold pigments, as shoppers increasingly prioritize ingredient-conscious choices.

#RushedMakeup shows that consumers are drawn to quick, ready-to-go routines that demonstrate how to look polished fast. #NailTechASMR reflects fascination with sensory content. #BeforeAndAfterFacelift signals that audiences are intrigued by dramatic visual transformations of cosmetic procedures. #SisterLockRetightening and #WigLaid highlights a strong interest in professional hair care expertise and the maintenance of intricate, high-effort hairstyles, while also capturing attention to precision and seamless style by showcasing how flawlessly wigs are styled and finished.

Sources indicate that the rise of scar sticks, PDRN serums, and liquid microneedling reflects a consumer increasingly invested in skin regeneration, barrier repair, and clinically backed ingredients. The portability and ease of scar sticks signal demand for convenient, targeted solutions, while liquid microneedling highlights appetite for professional-level collagen stimulation and enhanced absorption without in-clinic procedures. Growing interest in milk sunscreens signals demand for high-performance UV protection that feels lightweight, skincare-forward, and multifunctional. There’s also growth in matte lip balms, with Celine launching refillable matte lip balms accompanied by a special installation at Harrods on March 2.

Trending skincare brands reflect a shift toward clinically grounded, barrier-focused skin health paired with sustainability and device-led innovation. Genabelle and Tosowoong, both K-beauty brands, exemplify this movement: Genabelle develops science-backed, microbiome and PDRN-driven formulas designed to repair the skin barrier, while Tosowoong targets brightening, anti-aging, acne, and dehydration. At the same time, the growing attention around Shark’s CryoGlow LED mask, targeting acne, fine lines and puffiness, reflects a desire for professional-grade treatments that accelerate results, reduce inflammation, and replicate clinic-grade procedures. Meanwhile, Bolt Beauty’s biodegradable single-dose capsules and Yepoda’s K-beauty-inspired active formulations underscore the rising ingredient literacy of consumers.

On TikTok, the #FlawlessBraids hashtag is largely driven by hair stylists showcasing intricate braiding techniques, alongside AI-generated concepts of futuristic braiding devices that don’t yet exist — but imagine faster styling without sacrificing precision. Meanwhile, #NeonHairColor highlights bold experimentation and personal expression, while #GlowSunscreen reflects a skin-first mindset where protection and radiance are expected to work hand in hand. #ShadowLiner signals interest in detailed, technique-focused eye artistry, as creators break down application methods for more defined eye looks. #LipEssentials points to demand for streamlined, everyday lipcare that balances performance with convenience.

Recent findings suggest that the surge in beauty tools like red light therapy hats suggests that consumers are increasingly seeing the scalp as the biological foundation of hair quality, density, and longevity, embracing device-led, clinically inspired solutions they can use conveniently at home. Interest in ingredient-specific shampoo formulas featuring batana oil and amino acid, or those that are protein-free, reflects a more educated haircare buyer. Meanwhile, demand for hair smoothing serums points to a parallel desire for immediate polish and manageability. Together, these trends reveal a consumer who approaches haircare through targeted, science-backed and ingredient-conscious solutions.

Sources indicate that seapuri and Dr. Groot, both Korean brands, tap into the rising demand for scalp-focused, anti-hair loss care. Seapuri uses hydrating, mineral-rich formulas, including a water-based scalp serum to reduce hair loss and balance sebum, while Dr. Groot focuses on scalp-nourishing shampoos and targeted anti-hair loss solutions with a clinically inspired, results-driven approach. LED brands like CurrentBody, Shark, Solawave, Vym, Monastery and FAQ have also been leading the charge. Roz sits at the intersection of plant-based sustainability and professional performance delivering botanical-powered results that promote lasting scalp health. This positioning bridges the gap between the accessible, plant-based approach of California Naturals and the salon-quality focus of ISO Beauty — underscoring how consumers increasingly seek conscious formulations alongside visible, high-performance results.

On TikTok, hashtags like #BraiderOfTikTok and #BridalGlamLook are largely driven by professionals showcasing intricate techniques and polished transformations, suggesting that customers turn to the platform for inspiration. Meanwhile, #TryingNewHairstyles highlights a culture of experimentation and style switch-ups, while #SkincareMasks documents selfcare routines as part of an ongoing beauty journey. #RedHeadMascara points to growing demand for hyper-specific, shade-inclusive products, revealing that consumers are actively searching for solutions tailored to their unique features.

It has been revealed that there’s a growing interest in topical, bioactive wellness formats, with patches incorporating GLP-1s and NAD reflecting a shift to skin-applied solutions for metabolic support, longevity, and targeted physiological optimization. At the same time, consumers are searching for supplements such as oregano oil and L-theanine powder, pointing to continued demand for immune resilience and stress management through more traditional, scientifically informed formats. Cutting jelly, a Korean wellness supplement, is gaining traction for its appetite-suppressing, digestion-supporting, and fat-management proposition. Its popularity highlights a broader preference for convenient, flavorful, and results-driven wellness rituals. Collectively, these trends reflect a consumer mindset that blends experimentation with intentionality, seeking measurable benefits through both topical innovation and functional nutrition.

Industry observers note that the latest search trends show that consumers are treating wellness as a seamless part of daily life rather than a task. By brand, Javvy Coffee reflects a desire to turn everyday rituals into functional routines that boost physical performance, while Wellah signals interest in precise, results-driven nutrition for recovery and hydration. Lullabites points to a focus on restorative sleep supporting energy and clarity for the day ahead. Crisp Power highlights the rise of indulgent snacks that also meet fitness goals, and Magic Spoon shows that nostalgic, enjoyable foods are increasingly expected to deliver health benefits without compromising taste.

On TikTok, hashtags like #PinkAndPurpleHair and #PersonalizedFragrance are driven by owners embracing beauty as a form of self-expression and creativity, from bold hair colors and custom scents to playful hair accessories like bows. Trends such as #LipLinerPencil highlight a desire to explore colors and combinations for defined, polished looks. Meanwhile, content around #RetentionTips indicated that beauty consumers value expert guidance and skillful maintenance, ensuring they get the most out of specialized treatments such as lash extensions.

Consumers are going beyond basic hygiene in search of specialized products, like Epsom salt lotions for muscle recovery. The rising interest in PH-balanced body washes and fungal infection lotions highlights a shift toward dermatological wellness. At the same time, tools like the glass foot file are gaining traction, reflecting a consumer focus on at-home pedicures and skin maintenance. Meanwhile, the demand for Moroccan black soap underscores a desire for ‘heritage efficacy’, where customers seek out natural, ritual-based exfoliation to minimize synthetic chemical alternatives. These trends signal a more literate consumer who views the entire body — not just the face — as a landscape for clinical, preventative, and holistic care.

The rising search interest in brands like GoPure Beauty, QV Skincare, Diptyque, Susanne Kaufmann, and Bliss reflects a consumer shift toward the skinification of the body, whereby consumers demand high-performance active ingredients for use beyond their face. This behavior indicates a shift to clinical wellness, with shoppers balancing a need for dermatological efficacy and targeted solutions with a desire for the sensory luxury and ‘clean’ prestige offered by Diptyque and Susanne Kaufmann.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, content featuring hashtags like #HairExtensionInstallation and #BrowThreading are dominated by professionals sharing techniques, as more consumers use the platform to get inspiration or find services. In contrast, #MixedHairstyles and #HairExtensionsHack are mostly driven by consumers exploring practical options and DIY approaches to at-home styling. Elsewhere, #CrueltyFreeCosmetics reflect a growing interest in ethical and sustainable products, showing that conscious choices are increasingly part of beauty conversations online.

The rise in sweet fragrance searches shows consumers are craving comfort and indulgence. Interest in tomato perfume and milk fragrances points to a growing appetite for unconventional, nostalgic aromas that blur the line between food and scent. The emergence of edible perfume — designed to be safely consumed — signals a shift toward playful, multisensory experiences in which application extends scent beyond the skin. Meanwhile, demand for white floral perfume suggests that classic, elegant profiles continue to anchor consumer preferences amid experimentation.

The popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a shift toward luxurious and statement-making scents. Assaf, in particular, offers luxurious, often unisex fragrances that combine oud and incense with contemporary, international notes. The rise of Xinu, meanwhile, points to a growing interest in artisanal storytelling and plant-based ingredients. Also on the rise is XO Khloé, underscoring the continued power of celebrity-led fragrance lines.

The rise of #PinkNailDesign and #BraidsAndBows highlights playful, creative styles, while #GenZMakeup favors fresh-faced, natural looks with fun touches like graphic eyeliner, pastels, and faux freckles. The growth in #JLoMakeup is being driven by Jennifer Lopez’s Golden Globes look, which was inspired by the early-aughts supermodel glam that owners are eager to recreate. The growth of #FirstTimeBotox signals increasing openness and transparency around cosmetic procedures, as users frame treatments as relatable milestones rather than taboo transformations. Meanwhile, #HoneyHairMask highlights a parallel interest in plant-based, at‑home haircare rituals focused on nourishment and maintenance.

It has been revealed that consumers are going for self‑expression, playful motifs and hybrid styles when it comes to nail art. Searches for cat eye heart nails, pink cat eye nails, and cat claw nails show that consumers are blending shape‑driven trends with tactile finishes, embracing looks that feel both edgy and whimsical. Meanwhile, strawberry shortcake nails point to a nostalgia‑infused trend. The interest in Cynthia Erivo nails highlights how celebrity‑inspired nail looks can drive demand, with users translating red carpet or character‑driven aesthetics into their own manicure repertoire.

The top‑growing nail brands reflect a consumer shift toward at‑home expertise and expressive finishes. Heyhae’s popularity signals a desire for playful, design-forward polishes and tutorials that help customers translate looks for everyday wear. Gaoy and Rossi Nails underscore the rise of DIY gel systems and professional‑grade kits, revealing that consumers seek salon‑quality results at home. Jodsone’s ascent points to a craving for art‑centric, niche lacquer brands that stand out with unique color stories. Meanwhile, IBD Beauty highlights continued demand for reliable, performance‑driven products in the professional and enthusiast space, especially among gels and long‑wear finishes.

On TikTok, trending beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that blends identity‑driven aesthetics, routine conservation and sensory‑led selfcare. The popularity of #PastelGothMakeup demonstrates how consumers are embracing expressive beauty looks, using makeup as a form of cultural and creative identity. Hashtags like #SkincareRestock and #ShampooRoutine points to the importance of consistency and ritual. #StrawberryScents highlights an interest in nostalgic fragrance profiles, while #BasketballHairstyle reflects the influence of purpose‑driven, activity‑ready beauty content.

According to recent reports, consumers are getting creative thanks to the popularity of peel-off lip tints and liners. The rise of blue lip stain, which applies blue but reveals a pink or berry hue once peeled, speaks to the demand for color-shifting, pH-reactive formulas that feel personalized and surprising. Plumping lip liner reflects a desire for makeup that mimics cosmetic procedures, with consumers drawn to products that visibly enhance lip volume without injections. Meanwhile, plum mascara shows how consumers are exploring non-traditional but wearable color accents.

The top-growing makeup brands reveal a consumer shift toward inclusive design, minimalist aesthetics, as well as age and tool-specific solutions. Tilt Beauty reflects rising demand for accessible, user-friendly packaging and refillable formats that are sustainable. Sweed Beauty appeals to a growing audience seeking the no-makeup makeup look, through vegan formulations that deliver barely-there finishes for natural enhancement over heavy coverage. Maange demonstrates that consumers are investing in quality makeup brushes and application tools, signaling increased interest in the techniques behind the look, not just the formulas themselves. Meanwhile, Jung Saem Mool attracts those drawn to editorial-inspired, K-beauty artistry, and Prime Prometics caters to the needs of mature skin, emphasizing that makeup shoppers are increasingly seeking products that serve their specific life stage and texture needs.

The rise of #HairExtensionsTutorial and #TakingOutBraids highlights that people are actively seeking step‑by‑step guidance for maintenance and technique. #FrenchHairPin and #PurpleHairDye underscore a growing appetite for aesthetic experimentation and trend‑inspired looks, where tools and color become playful ways to express personal style. Meanwhile, #UltaHairSalon points to the influence of in‑salon experiences and professional authority in shaping consumer choices, with users looking to bridge DIY learning and expert execution.

Skincare products that blend restorative care, gentle technology and everyday indulgence are on the rise. The popularity of scar sticks and PDRN serums points to the advancement in regenerative treatments that support healing and skin repair. Tools like ultrasonic skin scrubbers highlight consumers’ appetite for at‑home derm‑tech devices. Also, melting lip balms and pore care are trending as consumers seek results‑driven everyday products.

Brands with ingredients-conscious efficacy, modernized wellness and at-home performance solutions are being sought after. Terra Lotus, powered by beef tallow-based care, signals a growing interest in animal-derived, nutrient-dense skincare rooted in traditional practices, as consumers seek richer, bioavailable alternatives to plant oils and lab-created moisturizers.

In a recent development, APLB and Genabelle continue to spike interest in science-backed K-beauty, especially products targeting hydration, brightening, and skin regeneration through actives like niacinamide and glutathione. Dermagist points to sustained interest in cosmeceutical-style anti-aging solutions. Finally, Shark Beauty’s expansion into skincare devices reflects the growing appeal of tech-enhanced and at-home treatments.

Consumers are eager to participate in viral beauty without overspending, as #AffordableLipOil and #AffordableMascara make strong cases for accessible versions of trendy, functional products. #ProfessionalHairProducts point to a growing appetite for salon-quality care. In contrast, #HydroDermabrasion reflects a rising interest for in-spa skincare treatments, as consumers turn to TikTok to understand the benefits of medical-grade exfoliation and glow-boosting facials. Meanwhile, #CranberryMakeup underscores the continued influence of seasonal and mood-based beauty aesthetics, as people experiment with rich, warm tones to express personal style.

Exfoliating foot masks and hand masks are on a spike, as consumers approach the treatments with the same ritualistic care traditionally given to the face. Vegan body wash and magnesium body butter reflect a shift toward wellness‑aligned, ingredient‑conscious products. Meanwhile, exfoliating body lotion bridges treatment and care, showing the consumer’s need for multifunctional products that improve texture and moisture in a single step.

Kate McLeod and Brown Sugar Babe offer sensory bodycare experiences, from exfoliating stones to whipped butters. Brands like Dettol and Noshinku show that trusted hygiene and germ‑defense solutions remain top of mind. Bend Soap Firm’s artisanal approach highlights the appeal of small‑batch, craft formulations.

It has been revealed that these top‑growing TikTok beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that values efficacy, personalization, real‑world practicality and community‑driven discovery. The popularity of #ScienceBasedSkincare and #SkincareApp shows that users are increasingly seeking data‑informed products and digital tools. At the same time, #LazyGirlSkincare and #ThinHairTips reflect a demand for simple, low‑effort solutions that fit into busy lifestyles or specific concerns. On the makeup side, #BlushLovers highlights the enduring appeal of color cosmetics.

It has been revealed that the surge in interest for marshmallow perfume and chocolate perfume reflects a continuous craving for gourmand, dessert‑inspired scents. The rise of rose vanilla perfume and bridal perfume suggests people are gravitating toward romantic and memory‑evoking fragrances. Growing searches for oil‑based perfume show an increased interest in long‑lasting and body‑centric scent formats, revealing a preference for fragrance that melds seamlessly with one’s natural scent and lasts longer than traditional sprays.

Industry observers note that matière Première takes on the farm‑to‑fragrance purity and minimalist luxury, with its raw material‑focused compositions. La Sultane de Saba Paris channels consumer interest with olfactory-inspired notes. Similarly, The Maker Perfume hints at a growing demand for identity‑driven scent choices over mass market fragrances. Meanwhile, legacy and designer‑adjacent brands like Hugo Boss and Penhaligon’s continue to draw attention for their heritage and status, even as they explore niche alternatives.

Sensitivity-aware routines, personal customization and ingredients‑led problem-solving beauty are growing hashtags on TikTok.

The popularity of #SensitiveSkincare indicates more people are seeking gentle, irritation‑free formulas. Meanwhile, #UnderratedSkincare suggests a hunger for hidden gems or under-the-radar products, meaning consumers are increasingly willing to explore beyond mainstream brands. The rise of #BlondeHighlightsOnDarkHair and #HairLoss captures demand for hair‑specific solutions and transformation content, as users look for guidance and community advice on challenging hair goals. Finally, #CoffeeSkincare points to the ongoing appeal of natural, functional ingredients, as people are drawn to the antioxidant and circulation‑boosting benefits of coffee in skin and hair routines.

It has been revealed that bold nails are back and it’s all about self‑expression and textured innovation with growing interest in statement cheetah print designs rooted in nostalgia and glamour, blending animal prints with modern finishes and clever color shifts. The appetite for animalistic styles continues with cat eye nails reflecting excitement around method‑driven finishes — using magnetic polish to create shimmering dimension that feels both futuristic and accessible. Water drop nails and junk nails are also making noise with sleek, sculptural texture for the former and a maximalist approach to the latter with oversized charms, clashing textures and extreme customization.

Consumers are leaning into at-home expertise and expressive finishes. Gaoy and MelodySusie highlight a growing investment in DIY tools like gel kits, lamps and drills. Nail Labo caters to a rising demand for precision and minimalist artistry, drawing from Japanese nail culture that prioritizes clean lines, quality materials and technical skill. Caudalie introduces a skincare-forward angle with its hand and nailcare rooted in antioxidant-rich formulations. Meanwhile, Ethereal Lacquer is capturing attention through its holographic, metallic and multi-chrome polishes, signaling that many nail consumers are seeking and collecting bold, light-catching finishes that double as artistic self-expression.

The popularity of #OilToFoamCleanser reflects growing interest in innovative hybrid formats, suggesting consumers are drawn to easy and elevated routines. #OilySkinHack points to a problem-solving mindset, where users seek shareable solutions tailored to specific skin concerns, especially shine and congestion. Meanwhile, #ManiInspo and #GlitterHighlighter showcase visual beauty through inspiration and self-expression, with consumers looking for aesthetic ideas that feel fresh, playful and mood-driven. Lastly, #EdgeControlFor4cHair emphasizes the demand for texture-specific solutions and culturally resonant beauty techniques.

Recent findings suggest that matte powder is trending, as consumers seek polished, smooth and filtered‑like skin finishes. The popularity of pink lip stain and lipstick pencil, meanwhile, highlights a tilt toward bold lip looks that are still accessible and day‑to‑day friendly. Techniques like tightline eyeliner illustrate how subtle definition is gaining traction, reflecting a preference for minimal effort with big impact. Contrastingly, the surge in black lip stains suggest that consumers are also embracing more daring, identity‑driven looks that go beyond enhancement.

According to recent reports, among the top‑growing makeup brands, there’s an emphasis on accessible, niche aesthetics and cultural authenticity across price points. BBIA’s K‑beauty roots and affordable, vibrant product lines show how makeup lovers are drawn to colorful products that promote self-expression. Kulfi Beauty’s South Asian-inspired, inclusive shade range underscores a demand for brands that acknowledge and celebrate underrepresented skin tones and identities. On the other end of the pricing spectrum, Hermès brings luxury craftsmanship and premium finishes to makeup, signaling that consumers also view beauty as a status and lifestyle experience. Meanwhile, Palladio Beauty and UCoolMe illustrate how ingredient-driven products and purpose‑driven formats (like lash clusters) are becoming non‑negotiable for many buyers.

Industry observers note that on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer behavior shift toward accessibility, self‑expression and targeted problem‑solving. The surge in #EyelashLiftAndTint showcases how users are seeking out tutorial‑friendly content and at‑home techniques to achieve salon‑level transformations. Meanwhile, #BraidingExtensions and #NailsDesignIdeas point to a growing appetite for creative styling and personalization in hair and nails. At the same time, #KojicAndTurmericSoap highlights the fascination with viral, ingredient‑centric skincare that promises visible pay-off through ‘miracle’ formulas. Lastly, #PinkLipLiner reflects a subtle shift from cool-tone nudes toward warmer, reddish-pink tones that add soft color while still feeling natural — indicating consumers’ evolving preference for makeup that enhances without overpowering.

Industry observers note that the rise of morning shed, the ritualized removal of multiple overnight beauty tools and treatments, highlights a growing fascination with stacked, intensive skincare routines that promise overnight results. Searches for face-lifting masks reflect a desire for visible tightening, while hydrogel’s jelly-like, cooling texture satisfies a craving for sensorial, soothing formats. Meanwhile, rising interest in milky toners and turmeric face creams shows demand for gentle nourishment and targeted actives, with turmeric specifically valued for its natural, hyperpigmentation-reducing benefits.

According to recent reports, by brand, Grace & Stella and Byoma each represent a demand for approachable, feel-good skincare — whether through playful formats like eye masks or barrier-repair formulas that emphasize maintenance and simplicity. In contrast, brands like AnteAge, Bioeffect and Medik8 cater to a results-focused audience seeking science-led actives like EGF and retinal, signaling rising trust in clinical, regenerative skincare that targets aging and skin renewal at a deeper level. Consumers are embracing a dual approach to skincare, blending routine-friendly support with targeted, high-performance treatments, depending on need, mood, or life stage.

According to recent reports, in the TikTok sphere, trending beauty hashtags are focusing on age inclusivity, professional-level prep, and tailored care for specific identities and beauty concerns. #BeautyOver60 spotlights content that speaks directly to mature audiences, as those aged 60-plus seek routines and products that speak to their evolving needs and celebrate aging confidently. #BridalSkinPrep, often used by makeup artists, reflects interest in expert-driven techniques that enhance makeup application, as consumers value the behind-the-scenes steps that create flawless, event-ready skin. Meanwhile, #CollegeHairstylist, #RedHaircare and #CeramideSerum point to highly specialized content — from on-campus hairstyling services to color-specific hair routines and barrier-supporting ingredients — illustrating a broader trend toward community-rooted expertise and ingredient-conscious skincare.

In a recent development, haircare is of increasing importance to consumers, as beauty focuses go beyond the surface to tackle cosmetic concerns at their root. The rise of DHT blocker shampoos and scalp serums signal growing concern around hair thinning and scalp health, with consumers turning to targeted treatments that address hair loss at its source. Interest in lightweight conditioners and hair UV protection highlights desire for gentle hydration and environmental defense, which avoids build-up and leans into skincare. Hair fiber powders are also rising, especially among young males, as consumers seek quick-fix solutions to thinning and receding, challenges becoming more prevalent in social dialogue.

Industry observers note that among haircare brands, there’s a consumer shift toward precision and wellness‑infused formulations. Cerave’s expansion into haircare underscores the demand for dermatologist‑approved, barrier‑support solutions — with ceramides and niacinamide anchoring formulas that consider scalp health as closely tied to hair health. Arey taps into a preventative and repigmentation‑focused niche by offering clinical systems to address greying hair, as more consumers seek anti‑aging hair solutions. Design Essentials and TGIN highlight a growing emphasis on texture‑specific haircare, delivering salon‑quality formulas for relaxed, natural and coily hair types. Meanwhile, Vichy brings its skin‑science heritage to hair with targeted treatments for dandruff.

Recent findings suggest that on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer shift toward efficiency, targeted solutions and hacks. The rise of #OnTheGoMakeup highlights how beauty routines are being compressed and adapted for busy lifestyles. #ChopstickCurls, referring to tight, defined curls achieved with ultra-thin rectangular-shaped wands, reflects consumer interest in niche, high-impact styling tools. Hashtags like #DepuffSkin, #OilySkinSolutions and #MicellarWaterHacks point to a demand for quick‑acting, problem‑solving formulas, especially those that tackle puffiness, oil control, or simplify skincare cleansing — reflecting an audience that wants visible change with minimal fuss.

In a recent development, in the evergrowing wellness space, consumers are leaning into metabolic health, enhanced performance and functional supplementation. The popularity of moringa supplements and probiotic shots reinforces interest in plant-based, gut-friendly solutions that offer antioxidant, digestive and anti-inflammatory benefits. As the links between gut health and other bodily concerns continue to emerge, consumers are turning to natural tools for internal balance and immunity support. Ketone and NAD supplements reveal that biohacking and longevity are still on consumers’ minds, as they seek ways to improve energy, cellular repair and cognitive performance through next-gen supplementation. Meanwhile, inferno Pilates lean into the high-intensity, hybrid fitness formats that combine strength with cardio — signaling a demand for wellness routines that challenge the body while delivering visible, fast-track results.

When it comes to wellness brands, Puori stands out for its ultra‑transparent, minimalist supplements that indicate a strong consumer demand for trustworthy quality and ingredient purity. Javy Coffee merges convenience and function by offering high‑protein, sugar‑free coffee concentrates, hinting that wellness is being woven into everyday routines as well as indulgent moments. Meanwhile, brands like VH Essentials focus on women’s intimate health with probiotic‑rich, lifestyle‑friendly formats, signaling a move towards specific wellness needs and gender‑tailored solutions. Lastly, Snap Supplements and Alaya Naturals emphasize science‑backed formulas, superfood blends and adaptogens, while highlighting how modern consumers are gravitating toward preventative, system‑focused wellness — gut, hormones, vitality — rather than generic multivitamins.

According to recent reports, fragrance notes like tonka bean, marshmallow and chocolate are doing the rounds this month, marking a shift towards gourmand scents that evoke warmth, nostalgia and emotional selfcare. The rise of skin perfume, specifically, suggests a desire for intimate, personal and subtle scent expression, via those that feel like an extension of one’s natural body rather than a bold statement. Overall, the convergence of edible sweetness and minimalist sensuality reflects a broader cultural movement towards self-soothing luxury and authenticity in beauty.

According to recent reports, interest in fragrance names like Penhaligon’s and Arquiste signals a craving for heritage, craftsmanship and historical storytelling, while brands like Fugazzi, Mind Games and Salt & Stone appeal to a modern, conceptual take on scent as identity and lifestyle. Together, they illustrate how consumers are moving beyond simple scent preference into fragrances that express intellect, emotion and personal storytelling. The blend of artisanal tradition with contemporary creativity underscores a desire for depth and meaning in luxury purchases.

On TikTok, hashtags like #BrideGlam and #GlitterLip highlight the appeal of high-impact, celebratory looks, whereby makeup becomes a central part of milestone events or cultural moments — favouring drama, glamour and transformation. #BoyPerm reflects a growing interest in inclusive and gender-diverse beauty trends, with more men engaging in expressive grooming routines that merge selfcare with style. Meanwhile, #ChristmasFragrance and #PistachioFragrance signal a desire for seasonal and gourmand scent profiles, outlining how consumers are embracing fragrance as a way to enhance mood, nostalgia and personal identity.

Industry observers note that when it comes to nail trends, there’s particular interest in visually impactful designs through experimental, DIY techniques. Styles like cheetah-print nails, cat-eye nails and camo nails highlight a demand for bold, expressive nail art. The rise of glass nails points to an appetite for reflective aesthetics that blend minimalism with more ethereal finishes for a polished yet fresh feel. Meanwhile, there’s been an influx of searches for nail art tools, suggesting that consumers are embracing the at-home manicure and shifting towards self-sufficient beauty routines with the potential for salon-quality results.

Among nail brands, there’s a strong appetite for individual expression, indie artistry and at-home manicures. Brands like KBShimmer, Death Valley Nails and Ethereal Lacquer reflect a growing preference for polishes that offer unique colourways, shimmer effects and limited-edition drops — highlighting a desire for collectable and distinct nail aesthetics. The popularity of Gaoy and Vettsy, both known for DIY-friendly gel systems and nail art tools, underscores a rising interest in nail artistry at home, where consumers are eager to replicate salon-quality results with accessible kits and tools.

Recent findings suggest that tikTok’s trending beauty hashtags reflect a consumer focus on practicality, preparedness and style-conscious experimentation. #SkincareWithSPF and #FrizzyHairProduct show that customers are increasingly seeking functional, protective solutions — prioritising formulas that address real-world conditions like sun exposure and humidity, with a preference for efficacy and daily utility. Hashtags like #TravelMakeupKit and #NailBeginnerTech reveal a desire for compact, beginner-friendly beauty tools that support on-the-go lifestyles and DIY techniques, especially among newer users entering beauty with simplicity in mind. Meanwhile, #BalletcoreNails highlights the continued influence of aesthetic subcultures, as consumers lean into soft, theme-driven self-expression, which blends elegance with trend-driven visuals.

Sources indicate that among the fastest-growing makeup trends, there’s a clear preference for long-wear performance and perfect complexions with a soft-focus finish. The rise of purple lip stain and tightline eyeliner reflects a move towards subtle drama — techniques and shades that add definition or intensity while still feeling wearable. Meanwhile, the growing interest in matte powder, matte blush and blur foundation points to a demand for shine-control and smooth, filtered finishes, which signal a shift away from the dewy trends of the last few years.

When it comes to brands, there’s an appetite for those offering bold aesthetics, inclusive branding and skin-conscious formulations. Vive Cosmetics and BBIA speak to a desire for high-pigment colour cosmetics that tap into Latinx and K-beauty influences, respectively. UCoolMe and Blink Lash, both known for their lash offerings, underscore a demand for eye-centric beauty and semi-permanent or low-maintenance solutions that elevate with minimal effort. Meanwhile, Oxygenetix taps into a rising preference for breathable, skincare-infused makeup, especially for sensitive or post-treatment skin — showing that performance and skin health are no longer mutually exclusive.

Industry observers note that on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags highlight a consumer focus on specialised education, age-specific needs and event-driven beauty goals. Tags like #CurlyHairEducation and #MakeupForOlderWomen reflect a growing demand for inclusive, tailored guidance, where users are seeking beauty content that respects diverse hair textures and aging skin. The popularity of #NanoTipHairExtensions and #WeddingDayLook shows that consumers are also investing in transformative, high-stakes beauty choices, particularly around special occasions or semi-permanent enhancements. Meanwhile, #CongestedPores points to the continued interest in skincare problem-solving, with users turning to platforms like TikTok for visible results, product recs and routine hacks that address common skin concerns.

In the skincare space, sensory experiences, targeted treatments and barrier-conscious hydration are among consumer trends. The popularity of milky toners and flavoured lip balms highlights a craving for multi-sensory, aesthetically pleasing skincare products that feel indulgent while delivering softness and comfort — often rooted in nostalgic or K-beauty routines. Meanwhile, cryo masks and hydrogel masks point to an interest in cooling, calming formats that offer instant relief and visible refreshment, especially for inflammation, puffiness, or post-treatment recovery. The rise of rosacea gel underscores a demand for dermatologist-informed solutions for sensitive skin conditions, highlighting a broader shift towards soothing, functional skincare that restores and protects the skin barrier.

It has been revealed that when it comes to skincare brands, there’s a consumer desire for clinical-grade efficacy, preventative care and products that align with specific lifestyle or skin needs. Epicutis and Medicube represent the rise of science-backed, treatment-oriented brands, appealing to consumers seeking dermatologist-aligned solutions for ageing, texture and sensitive skin concerns. Consumers are increasingly turning to science-backed and dermatologist-associated brands like Arey, Cerave, and Vichy, signalling a desire for clinically validated solutions for scalp and hair health. The top-growing brands in the space reflect consumer interest in innovation and self-expression. Wonderskin stands out with its cutting-edge lip stain technology, appealing to those seeking unique, long-lasting solutions. BBIA, a Korean brand, highlights the continued influence of K-beauty in shaping global beauty preferences. Lethal Cosmetics caters to bold, expressive consumers, while Tower 28 Beauty combines performance with gentle formulations and Mob Beauty addresses the growing demand for sustainable, refillable packaging.

The top-growing beauty hashtags on TikTok reveal a consumer focus on achieving aspirational looks while prioritising practical solutions. Hashtags like #VolumeHairstyle and #VolumeHairHack reflect a desire for transformative, high-impact hair trends paired with accessible tips and tricks. #LipcareTips and #HowToTreatAcne demonstrate the continued importance of skincare, with an emphasis on selfcare and targeting specific concerns. Meanwhile, #HolidayGlam captures the excitement for seasonal beauty moments, showcasing a blend of creativity and celebratory expression.

The top-growing skincare trends highlight a consumer focus on plant-based and heritage-inspired solutions. Beauty of Joseon and Illiyoon reinforce the rising interest in K-beauty brands, which emphasise gentle, heritage-inspired skincare through traditional ingredients like rice and lanolin. While brands like A313 and Rhode Skin cater to the demand for results-driven formulations, with a focus on high-performance solutions and research-backed products, respectively. Products such as collagen masks and castor face oil reflect a desire for targeted, restorative care that promotes both hydration and repair. The popularity of face taping suggests a rising interest in non-invasive, DIY techniques for achieving smoother, youthful-looking skin. Together, these trends underscore a preference for approachable, ingredients-led products that promise visible results and resonate with selfcare rituals.

This week on TikTok, key hashtags reflect a consumer interest in accessible, relatable beauty practices that fit seamlessly into everyday life. Themes of convenience, as seen with #FastMakeupLook and #EasyMakeupLooks, highlight a desire for streamlined routines that deliver polished results promptly. Personalised and curated aesthetics, meanwhile, are also gaining traction, as seen in tailored lip and nail trends such as #BrownLipCombos and #LipGlossNails. Additionally, social connection plays a role, with #CouplesSkincare showcasing beauty as a shared and enjoyable experience.

It has been revealed that the top-growing haircare trends and brands reflect a consumer shift towards plant-based, targeted solutions for specific hair needs, such as promoting growth and managing texture. Ingredients like onion and rosemary highlight a preference for botanical remedies rooted in traditional practices, whereas low-porosity hair treatments and flaxseed gel emphasise a focus on customisation and hydration, catering to diverse hair textures and porosity levels.
