Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta

📅 15 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mushroom fans: Bookmark this recipe immediately.
  • Sources indicate that A few helpful notes for pasta success: (1) While any pasta will work, egg-based noodles, like the fettuccine I recommend here, are the best complement to the sauce.
  • Find more fall favorite meals here: Weeknight Pumpkin Chili; Cream-ish of Mushroom Soup; Mushrooms au Poivre.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mushroom fans: Bookmark this recipe immediately. It will give you everything you want when you crave a creamy mushroom pasta as soon as the crisp fall air sets in. The hardworking trio of miso, Parmesan, and touch of soy sauce delivers an umami bomb of flavor that doesn’t overwhelm, but magnifies, the best of earthy mushrooms. Coupled with luscious noodles enrobed in a creamy (but not heavy) sauce, what’s not to love?

Sources indicate that A few helpful notes for pasta success: (1) While any pasta will work, egg-based noodles, like the fettuccine I recommend here, are the best complement to the sauce. The nests (Rummo and De Cecco are great accessible brands) cook far faster than standard straight pasta, almost as fast as fresh. (2) Don’t be afraid to season your mushrooms! Yes, I know this goes against all that we’ve learned about salting them too early in the cooking process, but just a bit of salt will get them going and releasing their water faster for eventual crisp-browned edges. Don’t be alarmed if you see a pool of water at the start of the mushroom cooking—that’s to be expected and just keep going until it evaporates. (3) Don’t forget to reserve plenty of pasta cooking liquid, which is critical to the eventual sauce’s success. I prefer transferring the al dente noodles from the pasta pot to the skillet, letting any residual water come with it (and to ensure you don’t accidentally drain away that liquid gold).

Find more fall favorite meals here: Weeknight Pumpkin Chili; Cream-ish of Mushroom Soup; Mushrooms au Poivre.

Cook 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests) in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions.

Meanwhile, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over high. Add 1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt and toss to coat evenly. Spread out into an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until mushrooms are starting to release their liquid, 2–3 minutes (do not be alarmed; there will be a lot). Continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until moisture is almost completely evaporated and edges of mushrooms are starting to brown, 6–8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium-high; add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, tossing often, until garlic is fragrant and golden, 1–2 minutes. Pour in ¾ cup dry white wine, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan with a sturdy spatula or flat-edged wooden spoon, and cook until wine is mostly evaporated (you should have about 1 Tbsp. liquid left in pan), about 4 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 2 Tbsp. white miso and stir until melted and combined. Slowly pour in ½ cup heavy cream, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan; simmer until thickened slightly, 2–3 minutes. Add 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce; season with freshly ground pepper. Taste and add more salt if needed.

In a recent development, using tongs, transfer pasta to mushroom mixture and add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Increase heat to medium and bring to a simmer. Cook, tossing constantly and adding ½–1 cup more pasta cooking liquid to reach desired sauce consistency if needed, until pasta is al dente and liquid has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.

Remove pan from heat. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup) to pasta and toss to combine. Season generously with more pepper; taste and season with more salt if needed.

Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan and pepper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The hardest part was having something as intimate and personal as a diary become public,” states Plestia Alaqad of her decision to publish her diary-memoir, The Eyes of Gaza. The book details the harrowing first weeks after October 7 in Gaza as a young Palestinian journalist. Alaqad studied upcoming media and journalism at Eastern Mediterranean University in Cyprus before returning to her home in 2022. Intending to educate the world about her city, she did not know she would end up reporting the first stages of the genocide.

According to recent reports, alaqad’s reporting situated herself as a voice for the ordinary. In the first few days, she spoke to her neighbors and local children. Her reporting appeared mostly on her Instagram account, which grew to a little over 2 million followers, with many of her images republished by the BBC, The Latest York Times, PBS NewsHour, and The Washington Post. Even through the chaos and the expulsion of over 100,000 Gazans in the first few days, according to UNHCR, which Alaqad also recounts in her memoir, there are moments of tenderness caught by her and everyday Gazans she would meet and talk to. Her style of reporting is grounded in a sense of familiarity, narrating the everyday in extraordinary circumstances. She made connections with people in a way that makes you feel like you were alongside her, drinking tea with the local tetas and jiddos, watching the violence and the world collapse around you.

Industry observers note that alaqad left Gaza for Lebanon, where she is completing her master’s degree. During the course of our interview, she spoke openly with me about the loneliness of the isolation of being a witness, forever changed by the devastation.

It has been revealed that one of my favorite things about Gaza is the people and the sense of community. For example, the relationship between my neighbors and I. I’ve been living in the Al -Waleed Building since I was almost four years old, and I know all my neighbors. Like Dana, who lived next door next to me—it was like having a sister and best friend nearby at all times. Whenever I needed anything, I just knocked at Dana’s door. If I needed help picking out an outfit, if I needed help replying to messages, even if I was just bored and I wanted someone to hang out with, it was always Dana who I turned to. There’s something about Gaza that just is home to me. There is simplicity and a love for life in Gaza that I haven’t seen elsewhere in the world. So being born and raised there always meant having loving and supportive people around me.

There’s more to us than being occupied. We’re full of talent and art we never got the time to make, because we’re too busy worrying if the people we love will still be alive tomorrow. That’s what pushes me to keep writing.

Recent findings suggest that I’m interested in writing and telling stories of people. I recently interviewed Renad Atallah and wrote a piece about her for The New Arab. Also, one of my favorite pieces I wrote was an interview with Alaa Abu Diab, a one-of-a-kind comedian, for The National.

As of recently, I started my newsletter on Substack, where I share a personal essay every week on Gaza, girlhood, friendship, and everything in between. My ultimate hope would be to tell stories about a free Palestine one day. And as a journalist, I’ll always see my work as incomplete without going back to Gaza and continuing to tell Palestinian stories from the ground. And hopefully work on an international level and tell stories of people who suffered because of war and conflicts in other countries.

I enjoy reading nonfiction books and memoirs because I love learning about people and their experiences. I remember reading Anne Frank’s diary in middle school.… I remember how it made me feel and the impact it had on me.

Sources indicate that I have also always been drawn to personal writings, like Franz Kafka’s letters and the letters between Ghassan Kanafani and Ghada al-Samman. I think I’m a very curious person by nature, and I’m interested in understanding what is happening in people’s minds, and if I get the chance to read strangers’ diaries, I wouldn't say no. That curiosity is something that inspired me.

Sources indicate that growing up, I always had a diary. It was me and my purple diary against the world.… For me, journaling has always been my safe space in the world. It’s the one place where I can write whatever I want without feeling judged. That’s honestly why I wanted to create Neya [Alaqad’s creative brand], which is an Arabic word that means intention. The first product will be a journal, of course, and it will come in four different colors. Each journal has a small, kind reminder on the hardcover and little sweet quotes throughout the pages because I wanted to create something that is personal and safe, something you would want to come back to and share your thoughts in. For me, journaling has always been where I can reconnect with myself. I hope Neya can become that for other people too: a small space where they can pause, reflect, and reconnect with themselves.

The hardest part was having something as intimate and personal as a diary become public. Something that was once only mine suddenly was in the hands of people from all around the world. I always try to think about the impact it could have on others, and I’m grateful that this time we get to tell our own stories rather than having our stories told on our behalf. I’m also grateful for the readers around the world who have read The Eyes of Gaza and are making the effort to educate themselves about Palestine.

Industry observers note that I often feel like I am living in two worlds. On one hand, I have the opportunity to do things that many people back home cannot access freely, such as pursuing my education and continuing my master’s degree. On the other hand, I carry the weight of knowing what is happening to my people and my land, without having any superpower to stop it.

According to recent reports, I always try to stay honest and true to myself, and I try to take people through this journey with me online. I share the contradictions, the pain, and the moments of hope. What it’s like trying to process the experience of having your homeland bombed, your city erased, and your people murdered, while also surviving and trying to make sense of the world outside. It is something that is difficult to put into words.

Recent findings suggest that it feels like time has frozen in Gaza, while the rest of the world continues moving forward. And for those of us away from home, we are constantly trying to live between these two realities.

Gaza is a place where contradictions exist side by side. You see unimaginable grief, but you also see people trying to find meaning and strength in the middle of that suffering.

Sources indicate that the Eyes of Gaza captures these contradictions. On one page, sadness may take over, while on another, hope emerges. Ultimately, I believe that when people experience powerful emotions, they are often moved to take action.

  • “Connery’s suits were considered relatively contemporary, because Anthony always had a very soft shoulder on his suits,” explains Elliot Mason, the director of business at Anthony Sinclair, which is no longer located on Savile Row, but still makes classic British suiting.
  • In a recent development, opting to dress James Bond in a Savile Row suit might seem like a no-brainer in hindsight, but the decision—and the cut of the suits themselves—still resonates more than 60 years later.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when Terence Young, the director of Dr. No, needed a suit for Sean Connery to wear for his debut as James Bond, he took him to see his personal Savile Row tailor, Anthony Sinclair.

“Connery’s suits were considered relatively contemporary, because Anthony always had a very soft shoulder on his suits,” explains Elliot Mason, the director of business at Anthony Sinclair, which is no longer located on Savile Row, but still makes classic British suiting. “Anthony liked to nip in the waist, so it gave that real hourglass silhouette to the suit, which really is quite timeless. And as was the trend at the time, the Connery suits all had a relatively high rise, double-pleated with English forward pleats, and most of his trousers had Daks button-tab adjusters on the side.”.

In a recent development, opting to dress James Bond in a Savile Row suit might seem like a no-brainer in hindsight, but the decision—and the cut of the suits themselves—still resonates more than 60 years later. Sinclair would make all of Connery’s suits during his nine-year run as James Bond, and his blend of classic British tailoring and of-the-moment influences would create a template for every Bond to come. With Robert Pattinson—a Dior ambassador and a guy with a reputation for adventurous style—chosen to take up the mantle in Bond 26, the question now becomes: what will he wear?

Tailor Anthony Sinclair fitting Sean Connery for one of the suits he wore in 1963’s From Russia With Love.

According to recent reports, ian Fleming, the author who created James Bond, spent a lot of time talking about what Agent 007 drank (Wolfschmidt Vodka) what he drove (Bentley convertibles, for the most part) and how he made his coffee (he was a dedicated pour-over guy), but, surprisingly, he never specified where the spy bought his clothes. As a result, for the last six decades, it’s been up to the directors and costume designers of the 25 previous films to create a newly introduced look for every successive Bond. In the Connery and Moore eras it was Savile Row suits. Timothy Dalton’s Bond wore Paul Smith. Brosnan was a bespoke Brioni guy, as was Daniel Craig, who also brought Tom Ford into the mix. At 6’1” to Craig’s 5’10”, with a leaner build, and a long track record of fashion-forward dressing, Pattinson has everything needed to reinvent Bond once again.

Sources indicate that “I’m pretty sure we’re going to see something quite different from Pattinson's Bond,” notes Matt Spaiser, the tailoring obsessive behind BondSuits.com and the author of From Tailors with Love: An Evolution of Menswear Through the Bond Films. “Pattinson is a different kind of actor, and he’s going to wear something that moves differently. Plus, he’s 18 years younger than Daniel Craig.”.

The actor playing Bond has a major influence on how he dresses—Daniel Craig, an adventurous dresser himself, was very hands-on with the wardrobe in his films—but Pattinson’s ongoing contract with Dior could also factor in. “Some of his Dior looks look somewhat like James Bond—he wears a great tuxedo—but I don’t think it’s going to tell us what he’s going to wear as James Bond,” Spaiser says. “He’s worn suits from other brands in other roles—like in Tenet, he wasn’t wearing a Dior suit—so I don’t think he's necessarily obligated to be wearing Dior as James Bond.”.

Daniel Craig, seen here in 2019 with then-Prince Charles on the set of No Time to Die, mainly sported sharp Tom Ford suiting in his later Bond films.

Recent findings suggest that another important factor that contributes to a latest Bond’s look is what’s happening in fashion whenever the film eventually gets made. “One thing that we've seen throughout most of the Bond eras is that he dresses in suits that are fairly traditional, but there's always some nod to the era that they’re in,” says Spaiser. “Sometimes they lean a little more into fashion, like when Roger Moore was wearing flares. That was something that I think they couldn't avoid without making Bond look too old-fashioned at the time.”.

Tone also plays an important role, and historically has ping-ponged between serious (Connery, Dalton, Craig) and more campy (Moore, Brosnan), but with Denis Villeneuve, the auteur behind Sicario, Blade Runner: 2049, and Dune in the director’s chair, the smart money isn’t on hovercraft gondolas and punny Bond girl names. A darker, more atmospheric milieu could make for an interesting complement to Pattinson’s taste for high-fashion.

If Mason were dressing Pattinson for the role, he indicates, he’d take a lead from his clientele, many of whom, like Bond, are well-heeled Londoners with a taste for expensive sports cars and well mixed cocktails. “The majority of our customers are reasonably conservative, and when it comes to fit, they’re sensitive to current trends,” Mason notes. As such, he’d opt for longer jackets, both single- and double-breasted, that are fuller through the body, and straight-leg pleated trousers. “It’s not that very, very slim fit that we'd seen for so many years, but it still needs to be refined,” he says. “I don’t think it would be appropriate to put him in wide-leg or baggy trousers. I just don't think it’s right for Bond.”.

Robert Pattinson, the latest 007, has been the face of Dior’s menswear for over a decade.

Given the intense scrutiny on every relaunch of the Bond franchise, and the tendency of fans to get worked up online over perceived mishandling of a beloved character, Pattinson, Villeneuve, and the film’s yet-to-be-announced costume designers have little room for error. Go too conservative and they’ll be accused of playing it safe; make Bond into a fashion guy, and they’ll incur the wrath of the traditionalists.

Recent findings suggest that “He needs to look current, but also timeless,” Spaiser states. “It’s a hard balance to find.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I haven’t made a meal in the French countryside in fall; but sometimes I dream, and these slow-cooked lentils are what I’d make in such a situation. Back in my American reality, it still makes an excellent dinner or hearty weekend lunch. Look for mild smoked Austrian or German sausages, which lean on mellow herbs and warm spices (sometimes, if you’re lucky, they’re also stuffed with a nutty cheese)—this style is already cooked to a safe temperature, but the casing’s texture is greatly improved when seared before reheating. If your shop only carries sweet Italian sausage or something like an apple-stuffed chicken sausage, both work in a pinch. What a treat it will be to actually finish off that gallon of apple cider you impulsively bought last week in the lentil-braising liquid.

More great fall recipes this way: Charred Cabbage With Sausages and Apples; Pork Chops With Green Chiles and Apples; Mustardy Cider-Braised Pork Chops.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.), turning often, until deeply browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Combine 1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 3 celery stalks, finely chopped, 1 large carrot, peeled, finely chopped, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in same pan. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring often and scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring, just until fragrant, about 1 minute.

It has been revealed that add 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1½ cups apple cider, 1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed, ½ cup finely chopped parsley, 3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to pan. Increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Cover pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until lentils are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed but mixture is still saucy, 30–35 minutes.

It has been revealed that uncover pan and stir in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. Nestle sausages into lentil mixture and add any juices pooled on plate. Simmer until sausages are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Top with parsley leaves and reserved celery leaves to serve.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

In a recent development, rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the issue could occur by Wednesday.

A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.

Recent findings suggest that massie's resolution also charges Hegseth with disregarding protection of civilians in wartime and suppressing the free speech of a U.S. senator.

Massie declared his intention to file the resolution as a matter of the privileges of the House.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., will now have to rule as to whether the resolution constitutes a proper question of the privileges of the House. There is precedent from prior instances when impeachment was found to be valid as it relates to the House’s constitutionally granted powers.

Sources indicate that he must schedule a vote to occur within two legislative days. Assuming that the speaker rules that Massie's resolution is privileged, the House could vote on the resolution itself, or on a motion to table it or refer it to committee.

In a recent development, if the House were to impeach Hegseth under this process, it would mark a historical anomaly. According to the Congressional Research Service, recent attempts to impeach an official as a matter of the privileges of the House have not resulted in approval of the resolution. In cases in which an official has been impeached, the House has nearly always chosen to conduct an investigation first.

Recent findings suggest that in an interview on Oct. 26, Massie put the chances of his resolution being adopted at 50-50.

In comments to reporters outside the Capitol after his floor remarks, Massie said he suspected some Republicans may back his resolution but he indicated he has neither asked for nor received any such assurances from any of them.

He predicted there could be some GOP support in the Senate if Hegseth is impeached and it goes to trial. He noted that if the trial does not start until 2027, any Republicans who might vote to convict Hegseth would presumably be joined by most if not all of a more sizeable Senate Democratic caucus.

According to recent reports, massie's odds of success for his resolution may now be greater than his previous 50-50 prediction given the results of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which gave Democrats control over both chambers in the next Congress — a vote motivated largely by opposition to the Iran war and its inflationary impact.

According to recent reports, the questions now are, first, how many House Republicans will defy President Donald Trump and vote to impeach Hegseth; and, secondly, how many incumbents who lost their reelection bids on Nov. 3, a cohort that is disproportionately Republican, might be absent for the impeachment vote?

Industry observers note that massie noted some Republicans who lost their reelection bids may feel freer to vote to impeach Hegseth. And he also said Republicans who were reelected and will have to face voters in 2028 may also think about how their vote on an impeachment resolution would reverberate politically.

Industry observers note that "It's going to be everybody's conscience, and then they'll have to live with that vote," Massie said. "And they're going to have to live with that vote two years from now if they're not part of the retirement caucus. And if they were part of the retirement caucus, what do they have to lose?".

Asked why he did not bring articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump, Massie noted: "I think the president needs to see one of — this is a metaphor — one of his horses shot out from under him, and then maybe he'll he will see things differently.".

If the House does vote on Massie’s resolution, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who is expected to become the House speaker in the next Congress, remarked on ABC’s “This Week” on Sunday that he would be a “hard yes” on it.

Sources indicate that hegseth has “got to go,” Jeffries mentioned. “The so-called secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe.”.

Most if not all House Democrats are expected to agree.

Last week, Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., the ranking member of the Armed Services Committee and its likely chairman in the next Congress, indicated in an interview with The New Republic that he would support Massie’s impeachment resolution, and he predicted it would be adopted.

It has been revealed that referring to Massie’s measure, Smith said, “By every estimation, it will pass and he will be impeached. And off that goes to the Senate. Then the Senate is legally required to spend all of their time dealing with that until it’s done with.”.

Sources indicate that "Every second Pete Hegseth remains at the top of the Pentagon, our servicemembers are at risk," Rep. Jason Crow, D-Colo., a senior member of the Armed Services Committee, remarked in a post on X on Sunday.

Industry observers note that also on Monday, Everett B. Kelley, the national president of the American Federation of Government Employees, a union that represents some 820,000 federal and D.C. government employees, sent a letter to House members urging a “yes” vote on Massie's Hegseth impeachment resolution.

The letter cited the risks Kelley noted the Iran war has posed to the lives of the Defense Department's uniformed and civilian personnel, and the missive noted Hegseth's stripping of workplace rights and protections for the department's civilians.

Sources indicate that "By adopting Rep. Massie’s resolution, the House can begin the long overdue bipartisan effort to reclaim its constitutional powers and authority, restore checks and balances, and take responsibility for the lives of military personnel and civilian employees that Mr. Hegseth’s capricious leadership has jeopardized," Kelley wrote.

According to recent reports, massie confirmed in mid-September his intention to file an impeachment resolution against Hegseth. But Johnson adjourned the House before the vote would have occurred.

Massie’s newly introduced resolution is substantially the same as his earlier one, with the same eight articles of impeachment.

The first three of these alleges that Hegseth’s conduct of the Iran war violated the War Powers Resolution.

Massie's measure says Hegseth prosecuted the Iran war without congressional authorization and in the absence of an attack on the United States or an imminent threat.

It has been revealed that further, the measure alleges that Hegseth continued the war despite the House and Senate adopting in June a concurrent war powers resolution calling for the withdrawal of U.S. forces from the fight.

And, the resolution states, Hegseth continued the Iran war after the expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period.

Massie’s measure further asserts that Hegseth:.

In a recent development, the House has only voted twice to impeach a member of the Cabinet. In 1876, Secretary of War William Belknap was impeached over allegations of corruption, and his abrupt resignation likely contributed to his acquittal in the Senate.

In 2024, the House voted 214-213 to impeach Alejandro Mayorkas, then-secretary of Homeland Security, for “willful and systemic refusal to comply with the law” and “breach of public trust.” The Senate dispensed with the charges without a trial.

To find the best zip-up hoodies on the market, I dusted off Transatlanticism and went on a deep dive. The good news is that the old classics are still good. The better news is that there's a lot of great competition to choose from.

Uniqlo’s no-nonsense clean aesthetic and low price point has made it a go-to for any menswear enjoyer looking for good style on a budget. While the brand excels at cashmere sweaters, T-shirts, and a slew of homerun collabs, the Japanese label’s sweats are criminally underrated. We’d go so far as to say that they should be talked in the same breath as brands like Champion and Sunspel. This zip up hoodie took us by surprise thanks to its comfy midweight, all-cotton fabric and solid construction. But the main selling point is the impeccable fit.

Because of the fabric, the feel, and the overall fit, this is my favorite zip-up hoodie by a sizable margin. It’s my most-worn hoodie and has yet to show signs of any fraying.

Sources indicate that hoodies were originally meant for sportswear, as warm up gear before a grueling game of football. And if you want to kick it in comfort while saving your pennies for booze and amuse bouche for the big game with the boys, the best budget zip up hoodie to buy is Hanes’ EcoSmart zip hoodie. The fit is spot on—relaxed, but not sloppy, comfy in the body and the sleeves without swallowing you like a sand pit.

In a recent development, the fit is impressive for the price, and the overall quality means you’re getting a little more than what you pay for. It’s not a hoodie that’ll last you for too long, but it is a good quality piece for just 15 bucks. And when other hoodies offer lesser quality and worse-fitting options for about the same price? The answer is clear.

It’s hard not to sing the praises of Reigning Champ, a brand that built its fleece empire on sweatpants and hoodies. It was a revelation for me, too—Abercrombie wasn’t a name I associated with hoodies, but after I saw this in person, I had to readjust my menswear word cloud.

Recent findings suggest that some of the best zip-up hoodies for men are made by a brand you never see in brick and mortar stores. Camber has been crafting the most durable sweats for decades, right here in America and have been the shining example of the difference between good quality and great quality. Sure, you have to order through an old-school web 1.0 website and wait for several weeks to actually get your hoodie. But trust us when we say that the relatively minor inconvenience is completely worth it.

Industry observers note that the heavyweight fleece is almost as thick as a leather jacket and can stand in as outerwear if you wanted it to. While other hoodies are washed to hell in giant industrial washing machines to reach a super soft texture by the time it gets to you, Camber’s actually require you to do the work yourself. It sort of feels like you’re being swaddled by an anaconda, which means if you’re a proponent of hard clothes like raw denim, you’ll like Camber’s hoodie a lot.

Cashmere zip hoodies, once the exclusive province of Silicon Valley unicorn founders and PJ-flying nepo babies, have been democratized, none better than Naadam's take. You know the brand for bringing thoughtful, sustainable cashmere pieces at “really, only that much?” prices. Its zip hoodie is as soft as it gets, with extra credit points awarded for coming in a classic fit (too many cashmere hoodies err on the side of slim) and six colors, including this decidedly handsome olive. Wear it on weekends, work-from-home Fridays, and long flights—even if it's just Economy+.

Shoutout to brother in arms Louis Cheslaw, GQ Recs contributor, whose writing for the newsletter Magasin put us on to young brand Cease. From seed to sewing, it's beefy 20-ounce cotton is fully American-made. Assembling the fabric vertically means the hoodie will shorten up to a slightly cropped, oversized fit. Act fast if you want some of the less-boring colors—they move fast.

Industry observers note that we can’t deny Russell Athletic’s contributions to the hoodie space. And while its formula has changed over the years, the new hoodies are still pretty good for the price. The fabric is soft and lightweight, and it’s available in a rainbow of colorways. Plus, if you’re looking for a hoodie with a little more length, this is a great option.

Bold graphics aren’t usually deemed classics, but Gap’s retro-leaning collegiate-style block logo has staying power almost as much as the Levi’s red tab. Add to that a wonderfully fluffy midweight fleece material and a tailored straight fit and you’ve got something you’ll see on moodboards for generations to come.

Champion’s Reverse Weave fabric is iconic for its nearly shrink-proof quality and almost unsettlingly rough exterior. Flip it to the inside and you’ve got a luxuriously brushed interior that’ll have you feeling like you’re melting into a cloud. Heads-up that pricing varies kinda wildly by size on Amazon.

It has been revealed that the secondhand market is chock full of navy-blue hoodies that have been sun-faded and beaten down with time. They'll cost you just as much as this Mfpen version, but will also fall apart faster than you can zip 'em up.

Industry observers note that les Tien's dedication to all things sweats results in a catalog of luxurious fleece and terry cloth with a modern approach. Featuring high-end Cobrax hardware, RiRi zippers, raw-edge hems and sleeves, and a heavyweight brushed fleece, no detail is phoned in.

The Real McCoy's is considered by many to be Americana repro wizards. This revival of an early 20th-Century hoodie is just one small piece of the brand's preservation prowess. It's made using beefy sinker-knit fleece, old-school Talon-style zippers, and vertical patch pockets.

A.Presse's chokehold on the menswear illuminati refuses to let up and it's pieces like this vintage-inspired hoodie that keep the pressure on. Based on very rare “after-hood parkas", this made-in-Japan hoodie features an idiosyncratic attached hood, super dense and lofty fleece, with artfully distressed details throughout.

Recent findings suggest that think of the zip-up as the pullover hoodie's elder brother, but with way more layering potential. In its most natural state, it can cuddle up to a matching set of sweatpants and a baggy tee with flair. (Top it off with a swanky necklace, crisp sneakers, and some stellar shades and you’re left with a fit on par with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at his tunnel-trotting best.).

In a recent development, unzipped and left open, it can also take on the role of a picture frame ready to display your sickest graphic tee—much like the cardigan, another treasure of 2000s fashion. Or make like a mid-Aughts garage band ironically donning corporate attire and wear your zip-up over a dress shirt and baggy tailored trousers, a high-minded fashion move with a jolt of kooky Scandinavian cool.

According to recent reports, style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Sources indicate that our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

It has been revealed that to kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

We lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

It has been revealed that across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally new to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

In a recent development, whatever your preferences, whatever your style, there's bound to be a superlative version on this list for you. (Read more about GQ's testing process here.).

We Know How Sunrise on the Reaping Ends. That Doesn’t Change Its Impact.

📅 20 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Spoilers below for The Hunger Games books, including Sunrise on the Reaping.
  • Re-reading the original The Hunger Games series in preparation for this review, I started experiencing nightmares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Spoilers below for The Hunger Games books, including Sunrise on the Reaping.

Re-reading the original The Hunger Games series in preparation for this review, I started experiencing nightmares. Despite my generally overactive imagination, I would not call this normal. I read a lot of fiction, much of it politically prescient if not outright dystopian; if everything I consumed brought on such sleep paralysis demons, I’d call a doctor. But I shouldn’t be surprised that, now, Suzanne Collins’s young-adult trilogy began seeping into my subconscious, 15 years after I’d first turned its final page—especially considering that it’s now the latest in her series to become a feature film.

The lead protagonist in Collins’s trilogy, Katniss Everdeen, spends the entire series battling such nightmares as the death toll escalates around her. After volunteering as a tribute in the Capitol’s annual Hunger Games, pitting children against each other in a fight to the death, her already difficult life in District 12 becomes outright dangerous. She inadvertently sparks a rebellion. She leads that rebellion. She loses countless loved ones. Those of us who read and adored the series know how it ends, but even those unfamiliar with Katniss’s struggle can take an educated guess. Protest rarely goes unpunished.

I can’t claim to have experienced anywhere near the trauma Katniss undergoes throughout Collins’s trilogy, but I have aged considerably since I first read those books, and what struck me most as I re-encountered familiar passages was how present they still felt. I’d expected some nostalgia whilst leafing through The Hunger Games, Catching Fire, and Mockingjay, and the same when I’d pick up Collins’s latest installment in the franchise, the prequel novel Sunrise on the Reaping. I had not expected to feel so disturbed. Or so furious.

According to recent reports, this is the crowning achievement of Sunrise on the Reaping, which succeeds in the near-impossible task of making an well-trodden story feel as intimate and visceral as its predecessors. Reaping is the fifth Hunger Games novel and the second prequel installment after The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, which chronicled the youth and radicalization of the future president of Panem, Coriolanus Snow. (Like the original trilogy, Songbirds was adapted into a hugely popular Lionsgate film in 2023, and Reaping’s own adaptation landed in 2026.) Reaping surges forward a handful of years, set nearly a quarter of a century before Katniss’s own Hunger Games.

The story centers on Haymitch Abernathy, a beloved figure in The Hunger Games trilogy, in which he plays the role of the embittered if endearing drunk whose previous Hunger Games victory sets him up as mentor to Katniss and her District 12 partner, Peeta, for their own. In Reaping, Katniss and Peeta have yet to be born, but a young Haymitch knows their parents well. Here, Collins does a remarkable job of delivering what fans would call devastating “lore drops,” but she does so, for the most part, without resorting to cheesy or unnecessary Easter eggs. These minor characters—including Katniss’s parents, Burdock Everdeen and Asterid March—serve a clear purpose: to ground Haymitch in a familiar-but-reoriented District 12, where rebellion is yearned for but rarely acted upon.

According to recent reports, one of the few characters willing to risk their wellbeing in pursuit of justice is Lenore Dove, Haymitch’s girlfriend and a descendant of the Covey, a group of former nomads whom readers will recognize from Songbirds. Her conviction, her music, and her love (“like all-fire,” she claims, one of several Covey expressions employed throughout the book) steers Haymitch to her aid at the annual reaping ceremony, during which child tributes are selected for the Hunger Games. This year is a Quarter Quell, and the Capitol will demand twice as many boy and girl tributes as in an average year. After an unexpected execution takes place in the District 12 square, Haymitch finds himself rounded up with three other tributes and sent to spar for his life in the Gamemakers’ brutal arena.

According to recent reports, this is, of course, not a spoiler: Haymitch wins. Collins first described Haymitch’s victory way back in 2009 with the release of Catching Fire, during which Katniss and Peeta watch a recap video of Haymitch’s Quarter Quell. Through Katniss’s eyes, the young Haymitch comes off as “snarky. Arrogant. Indifferent.” But what Katniss doesn’t know is that the footage she’s watching has been heavily edited to reorder the timeline of events in the arena, and to remove Haymitch’s repeated efforts to undermine the Capitol. When he wins the games, he does so not as a ruthless survivor, but as a rebel attempting to break the arena itself. And when he returns home as a reluctant victor, he pays for his revolution a hundredfold.

We already knew from Catching Fire that, mere weeks after the Quell, President Snow orders Haymitch’s mother, brother, and girlfriend to be killed. But it’s something else entirely to experience those deaths on the page. In Sunrise on the Reaping, this mother, brother, and girlfriend are no longer nameless extensions of Haymitch himself; they are characters we’ve come to know (named Willamae, Sid, and Lenore Dove), whose deaths we dread despite their inevitability. Our anticipation does not ultimately erase our pain, just as pre-grieving an ailing loved one does not ultimately erase their loss. Collins understands this well, and she uses our emotions to target our instincts for both ignorance and apathy.

Sources indicate that in the end, Haymitch’s own assumed apathy cannot hold. He drives away his friends and few remaining neighbors, turning to “sleep syrup” and rotgut liquor as he’s tormented by violent memories and recurring echoes of “The Raven” by Edgar Allen Poe, which, in the world of Panem, has been passed down through the generations to become Lenore Dove’s “name poem.” In Poe’s famous 1845 poem, an unnamed narrator mourns the death of his lover, his “lost Lenore.” He is caught between two dueling desires: the temptation to forget Lenore and the desperation to remember her. His late-night visitor, a raven who only repeats the word “nevermore,” insists upon remembrance, driving the narrator to conclude that only madness awaits him.

Haymitch makes a similar conclusion—for the time being, anyway—as he wakes half-drunk from nightmares but stays alive, Lenore Dove’s final wish having “condemned [Haymitch] to life.” (She begs that he not let another sun rise on a reaping day, thus giving the book its title.) And though the word-for-word replication of “The Raven” in Sunrise on the Reaping is one of Collins’s few missteps—later eliminated by the movie adaptation—drawing the reader away from Haymitch’s world, the poem nevertheless carries a deeply poignant message.

According to recent reports, thematically, much of Sunrise on the Reaping is about propaganda, and specifically how truth is manipulated to trigger an audience’s emotional response. The Capitol Gamemakers edit footage of Haymitch to confirm what Capitol residents already want to believe about him—that he is a charming but ultimately dangerous rascal—and to ignore what does not suit their “logic.” As Plutarch Heavensbee (another character from the original trilogy) tells Haymitch and his allies, “People have an emotional response to something, then they come up with an argument for why it logically makes sense.” That explains the so-called “necessity” of the Hunger Games themselves: By convincing the Capitol residents to fear and deride the Districts, and the Districts to fear and covet the Capitol, the Capitol citizens are able to stomach the Hunger Games as “for the greater good”—and the Districts ultimately succumb to the resulting authoritarianism. History, as they say, is written by the victors.

But while propaganda is indeed a form of storytelling, there is a chasm of difference between twisting stories with malicious intent and preserving them for posterity. Collins’s use of “The Raven,” in addition to numerous other songs and poems popular amongst the Covey, is a testament to that fact. That a poem from 1845 would exist, in its entirety, numerous centuries in the future—having survived the collapse of North American society and the building of a totalitarian government bent on killing children—is something of a wondrous idea to behold. It is also a nod to the strength and resilience of the Covey themselves, who have taken care to maintain these stories despite the Capitol’s relentless and well-documented censorship.

As in Mockingjay and Songbirds, Sunrise on the Reaping ends with an epilogue. This final chapter leaps decades into the future, taking place in the years after Mockingjay and its siege on the Capitol. When Katniss and Peeta choose to compile a post-war “memorial book,” Collins writes that Haymitch is not initially interested in contributing. “What use?” she writes, from his perspective. “What point? To relive all the loss. But when Burdock’s page came up, I had to mention him showing me [Lenore’s] grave. And I felt compelled to tell them about Maysilee Donner, former owner of the mockingjay pin. And how Sid loved the stars. Before I knew it, they all came tumbling out: family, tributes, friends, comrades in arms, everybody, even my love. I finally told our story.”.

According to recent reports, haymitch realizes that forgetting was never really an option. It wasn’t an option for the narrator of “The Raven,” nor is it an option for him. Choosing to forget would be capitulating to a system that manipulates such forgetfulness for power-hungry aims. Intentional amnesia, learned apathy—both would be an abdication of love.

15 years after Mockingjay was released, I needn’t wonder why the series brought on refreshed nightmares. Authoritarianism is not a fictional threat. It has not been dreamed up for our entertainment or titillation. It is here and present and bloodthirsty. As with the entirety of The Hunger Games saga, Sunrise on the Reaping keeps this truth close to its heart, which is why—even for a book for “young readers”—its story is so difficult to absorb.

Yet Collins makes it clear that the war against injustice did not start or end with Katniss Everdeen. Before her was Haymitch Abernathy. Before him was Lucy Gray Baird, of The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. She learned her political anthems from the Covey, who learned them from their ancestors of yore. Stories, passed down through generations—each of them sowed the seeds of revolution that are sparked during Haymitch’s Hunger Games and ignited during Katniss’s. Dystopian literature like Sunrise on the Reaping is not a manual for effective protest, nor a crystal ball predicting the future. It is fiction and should be treated as such. But it can serve an essential purpose, one that Collins has not lost sight of in her decades of Hunger Games books: Fiction keeps close what we might otherwise deign to forget. It reminds us of what we stand to lose. And, at its best, it stirs us to pick up the fight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gloria Steinem’s life, work, and legacy were celebrated this week, as many gathered at a memorial service for the feminist activist in New York City.

The celebration of life took place at the Park Avenue Armory and came two months after Steinem’s passing at age 92.

Among those who came together to pay their respects were former United States first ladies Michelle Obama, Hillary Clinton, and Jill Biden—as well as Chelsea Clinton, Diane von Furstenberg, Meg Ryan, Lucy Liu, Emma Watson, Marisa Tomei, and Mariska Hargitay. In total, there were about 1,000 invited guests, all who were encouraged to donate to Gloria’s Foundation, which aims to preserve Steinem’s Upper East Side brownstone on East 73rd Street as a permanent archive and center for feminist organizing.

Rather than a somber service, the memorial was a joyful, music-filled celebration titled “It’s Steinemite!” Cynthia Erivo sang John Lennon’s “Imagine,” Cyndi Lauper performed “Girls Just Want to Have Fun,” and Kathy Sledge of Sister Sledge closed the event with “We Are Family,” joined by Lauper and Gloria’s Choir.

Recent findings suggest that for the evening, attendees coordinated in all-black ensembles—but it certainly wasn’t your average funeral attire. Clinton wore an elegant pantsuit—one of her favored looks. Obama was so chic and cool in a cropped blazer and a pleated skirt with a silky sash and golden accents. And Biden went for a fun, high-fashion ensemble that included Schiaparelli’s black Corsini suit jacket with asymmetric gold buttons.

If she could’ve looked into that crowd of incredible women, Steinem would’ve been endlessly proud.

While winter technically starts on December 21, we’re calling it now: the season has officially begun. We feel confident in this pronouncement because, here in New York, all around us, jackets are finally manifesting. On sidewalks, in subway cars, hanging on crammed racks at the entrance of restaurants, on the backs of stylish passersby—everywhere we look, there are trenches, puffers, shearlings, bikers, blousons, sleek gorpy jackets, and so many more. Every shape, color, fabric, and mood a person can imagine is represented by a fetching piece of outerwear. Naturally, of course, we have some thoughts on what will be crowned the coat of the season. With that in mind, we asked Vogue editors around the office to take a stab at what they think the hottest coat of the winter 2026-27 season will be. Here are a few very educated guesses.

“In the spirit of the forthcoming Met Gala, a coat that is more than ordinary. Caroline Bille Brahe is brilliant at taking a classic, like a winter tweed or a classic duffel and working her magic on it by adding strong shoulders and a yoke, or storybook decorations.” —Laird Borrelli-Persson, senior archive editor.

Caro Editions Caro wool coat in brown and green check, $1,505Caro Editions Thea wool coat in navy, $1,880.

“Conner Ives certainly did not invent the fur-trimmed chinoiserie coat, but his spring 2027 runway—plus its cadre of celebrity fans—sent everyone from the ladies who lunch to the louche downtown set clamoring for opulent outerwear. Don’t have six grand for one of Ives’ coats? There are already plenty of mass market interpretations in the works—plus a host of enterprising TikTokers sharing how to make your own.” —Hannah Jackson, senior fashion writer.

Connor Ives Reconstituted Vintage Fur and Silk Robe Coat in Black, £6,500.

Phoebe Philo funnel-neck jacket.

According to recent reports, “Coat necklines have been going higher and higher every season, so this winter, I predict the full-on funnel neck coat will be huge. I love how structured-yet-sleek the silhouette is. Phoebe Philo has luxe trench or leather versions, but there are also affordable ones too, like this gray Mango wool style. And the best part? They cover your neck entirely—meaning, one less layer you have to pile on in the winter months.” — Christian Allaire, senior fashion and style writer.

Phoebe Philo Cropped Trench, $2,600Phoebe Philo Swaithe Jacket $8,500Mango 100% Wool Funnel-Neck Coat, $209.99.

“As a Prada devotee, I saw this jacket go down the runway back in January and was immediately obsessed—it was pure Prada: subversive, distinctive, slightly off-putting and totally amazing. Its classic khaki cotton edges are fraying and crumbling away, revealing hints of traditional houndstooth at the hems and seams (and, in a particularly brilliant move, replacing the triangular logo at the yoke). But it’s also the most classic of shapes, easy to wear with practically anything. An amazing coat, 10/10. The only drawback (for me, at least) is that five-figure price tag. At least it’s a nice round number …?” —Max Berlinger, senior fashion news editor.

Prada Bonded Devoré Cotton Coat, $10,000.

“I’ve been wanting a lightweight plaid mackintosh for a minute now. I want something really long and with a classic approach to the pattern, and I found this on Massimo Dutti last week. I’ve been seeing these out on the streets a bit, it’s just such an easy way to add a little energy to an outfit, especially if you tend to wear darker colors (like me).” —Max Berlinger, senior fashion news editor.

Massimo Dutti Long Plaid Trench Coat, $490.

Industry observers note that “There is no more dominant jacket style than the mockneck bomber at this very moment—and you can thank Phoebe Philo for that. Still, despite her undeniable influence, whether the jacket is suede, leather, or technical, the most important part is the uber-studied, ultimately effortless Olsen tuck.” - Alexandra Hildreth, fashion news writer.

Phoebe Philo Rib Neck Black Leather Jacket, $8,000 Nour Hammour Quince Soft Suede Jacket in Mocha, $1,885Cos Leather Mock Neck Leather Bomber Jacket, $549.

It has been revealed that “Decadent, novelty overcoats are causing a frenzy. They might not be the most practical (or keep you very warm, for that matter), but they sure will make the outfit. They range from Colleen Allen’s velvet opera coats to Kallmeyer and Chan Luu’s jacquard dusters. Special shoutout to the Conner Ives vintage fur-trimmed satin coats that have been breaking the internet. Even Nour Hammour’s shearling and faux fur-trimmed coats are making outerwear a little more extra this winter. Here’s to making the everyday more extraordinary or, simply put, making your coat the look.” —Madeline Fass, fashion director, Vogue Shopping.

Nour Hammour Sophie 90s Leather Jacket, $2,120Kallmeyer Henri Floral Metallic-Jacquard Coat, $2,120Colleen Allen High Collar Velvet Coat, $3,000.

“The Vogue girls cleared house and won at Arma’s mahjong night a few weeks ago, which means that a few of us will be wearing our field jackets for the next few months. But while we may have won our jackets, the brand has been on fire since their presentations in New York and Paris last season. In fact, eagle-eyed Vogue.com readers may have even clocked their leopard coat, which has been photographed by Phil Oh multiple times in each Fashion Week city. But I like how the field jacket feels oversized and casual enough to wear with a plain sweater or even with a dressier jacket.” —Irene Kim, editorial production manager.

Arma Maeve Leather Field Coats, $1,550.

“Now that we’ve dredged all that we can from grandma’s attic, I think the next place to pull from is another house … the house of god. Stay with me, here: I think with Tom Ford’s Cry to Heaven on its way, and Pope Leo’s cultural dominance, we’ll see some monastic silhouettes beginning to emerge. Think the buttoned and buckled capes of Lanvin and Ann Demeulemeester, Nanushka's cheek-grazing collars, and the ecclesiastical severity of Mame Kurogouchi or Max Mara’s fall 2026 collections. It doesn’t have to mean austere—I love the drama of a mass! More like medieval monk meets modern minimalist, let’s say. I particularly love this La Veste Veste red and black cape that feels made for delivering the best homily of your life.”.

“I’ve also come to embrace the bitchy little blazer—The Gilded Age’s Louisa Jacobson being a big reference here. She loves some sexy Tom Ford suiting with a sharp-as-hell lapel. Upcoming kids on the block, Catalogue NYC are making slim, gently cinched versions while Antwerp’s La Collection offers up decadent texture with their Margaret blazer. Brenda from accounts, this is not.”.

“Despite their more tempered winters, Spanish women really know how to do good outerwear. And La Veste (which has been hosting a pop-up in Fresh York) transitioned from a summer of sparkly short-shorts and circus tent-striped sets into sumptuous, candy-colored wool blazers and car coats. Violet, chartreuse, and funky combo stripes abound! 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a big, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

In a recent development, bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

Sources indicate that heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.).

Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

It has been revealed that remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Abercrombie & Fitch’s resurgence has been well documented, and the brand indicates no signs of slowing down. Alongside its familiar mix of timeless staples, contemporary silhouettes, and archival-inspired pieces, Abercrombie has introduced YPB, or Your Personal Best: a dedicated line of performance apparel designed to bring the same considered approach to the gym as it does to the rest of your wardrobe.

Industry observers note that comprising everything from tees and tanks to shorts and jackets, YPB reflects Abercrombie’s ability to evolve while staying true to its heritage. The collection makes a convincing case for performance wear that goes beyond the usual sea of uninspired basics and head-to-toe Lycra. It’s also versatile enough to seamlessly move from a strenuous workout to the everyday wardrobe rotation. To put the collection through its paces, we’ve styled three looks that show just how far YPB can go.

Recent findings suggest that I am a chronic overheater so my gym outfits always reveal a bit of skin. (It’s also a vanity thing so I can see my muscles at work when I’m getting after it.) This vintage-inspired muscle tank looks like some of the actual vintage tees that I’ve taken a pair of scissors to without a stranger’s set-in stains. I have a lot of hair that gets in my way so headwear is a must when working out. A bandana is a nice throwback to the classic bodybuilder era and unlike a hat, it does a better job at soaking up the sweat so it’s not dripping down my face.

According to recent reports, the standout of this outfit is the shorts. Compression lined, they’re about as long as I’d go for shorts clocking in with a five-inch inseam. They have a discreet pocket in the liner to store my phone, and they're tight enough so my device doesn’t go flying out when I’m doing high knees. Plus, they’re stretchy enough for putting ass to grass on a squat without risking a NSFW tear between the cheeks.

Sources indicate that I’ve come to learn that recovery days are not only a blessing but a necessity. But they don’t necessarily mean you have to waste away on the couch all day. My active recovery days involve a lot of walking, and that means my workout shorts make an appearance once again. I can’t deny their comfort factor, and it’s hard to beat a sweater-and-shorts combo, an outfit beloved by my favorite A-listers.

It has been revealed that the sweater was a quarter-zip with an elastic waistband for a more streamlined, tailored fit. And if I’m walking a little too briskly, the top easily comes off to reveal a staple graphic tee in my wardrobe.

In a recent development, finally, I put on some pants! I don’t make it a habit to wear sweatpants out casually, but sometimes the weather calls for it. Hike ‘em up a bit and show off some crisp white socks, a style swerve I saw once and couldn’t help but copy.

Recent findings suggest that the staple of this outfit is the heavyweight jacket. Its water-resistant lining keeps me dry when the meteorologists get the forecast wrong, and it’s lined to keep me warm as the days get shorter and the nights get longer. The two-way zipper also allows for some extra mobility, and it won’t bunch up when I sit down like so many other parkas.

Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (422 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior.
  • More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.
  • Recent findings suggest that preheat oven to 425°.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Recent findings suggest that preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Industry observers note that whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Recent findings suggest that arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a substantial pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

  • According to recent reports, cecilie Bahnsen has a cult following for a reason: the Danish designer’s major blooming dresses and dedication to sporty, easy balletcore have been collected in droves by fashion far and wide.
  • In a recent development, for the occasion, Bahnsen spent half a year designing the collection and also collaborated with her friend Fumiko Imano, the artist, to shoot the campaign in Sweden amidst a picturesque landscape.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, cecilie Bahnsen has a cult following for a reason: the Danish designer’s major blooming dresses and dedication to sporty, easy balletcore have been collected in droves by fashion far and wide. So when Uniqlo came calling for her to design a second collaboration, it was time again for the designer to take the reins and merge her playful girlish Scandi style with the utilitarian wearability of the Japanese giant. The collection, which includes womenswear and childrenswear, puts a focus on cozy winter wardrobe dressing and is available now. In it, Bahnsen is rethinking and retooling the classic winter fleece.

In a recent development, for the occasion, Bahnsen spent half a year designing the collection and also collaborated with her friend Fumiko Imano, the artist, to shoot the campaign in Sweden amidst a picturesque landscape. “It was very much about sisterhood, the journey you do of exploring together, and inspiration also from when I’m in the countryside with my son, and we collect flowers, and how we kind of, he sometimes pinned them on his jumper,” Bahnsen tells ELLE of the upcoming collection. “I think it was really kind of that romantic or nostalgic feeling that I wanted to put into the collection. And then there was also this notion of just working with one fabrication and working with the fleece for winter and how you can work this as layering.”.

While Bahnsen in particular is known for her flouncy babydoll dresses, when it came to her second collection for Uniqlo, she tells us it was all about “refinement and balance and creating beautiful kind of everyday pieces.” Her personal favorite piece of the lineup is the fleece in the palest shade of soft pastel pink, embroidered with small flowers. “For me, the fleece is such a classic layering piece,” she indicates. She’s already been wearing it herself for countryside outings. “There’s romance and nostalgia to pink, and I think with this collaboration, it was nice to do the fleece in pink,” she says. “Showing that it could have that femininity to it was special, and it is also that right tone as a super soft pink that I love.”.

Sources indicate that the entire collection is designed to be layered, and the fleece is at the center of it. There’s a cropped fleece vest, a sheer long T-shirt printed with subtle bouquets of flowers, a floral-embellished fleece skirt and matching socks, gloves, and hats. Bahnsen herself recommends taking a cue from her own runway shows. “I always love a big jumper or a big fleece over a poof-y dress,” she notes. “It has both a super boyish vibe to it but also a princess-y, romantic feeling, too, so I love those kinds of contrasts between each other.”.

“These are pieces that you want to not just to work for one season, but to be timeless; it’s become about the perfection of these small details that makes it unique and maybe more romantic than what is normally in the Uniqlo collection,” adds Bahnsen. “I feel like the palette has a really Scandinavian winter tone to it, so how do you balance this soft pink into the darker blacks and blues, and kind of build it up, not in a monocomatic way, but really putting the tones and the layering together.” It’s definitely a chicer way to stay warm. The designer’s latest is the ultimate study of form and function.

How the ‘blue tsunami’ crested in North Carolina
